definition_zh: 质量；品质；特性；优质；音质
definition_en: how good or bad something is when judged against others of its kind; a feature that belongs to a person or thing; a high standard of excellence; the character of a sound
core_image: 一块被反复打磨的旧木料，纹理清晰，手感沉实
scene: 调音师把耳机贴紧耳朵，反复听同一段录音，判断那台旧钢琴的声音底色。 The quality of the piano's tone surprised the young tuner.
sceneCN: 这里 quality 是「声音的独有底色」（第 5 个义项：声音的特质与音质）；句意为那台钢琴的音色让年轻的调音师吃了一惊。画面里可留意：耳机、谱架、被手摸得发亮的琴键。

pos.zh: 质量；品质；特性；优质；音质

derivatives.zh: quality 换成 -itative，指「定性的、与性质有关的」，与定量相对
qualitative 加 -ly，指「从性质上、定性地说」
同出拉丁词干，指使合格、取得资格，是 quality 的动词同族形式

senses.title: The standard of something
senses.definition: how good or bad a thing is when it is judged against other things of the same kind
senses.definitionCN: 把某物与同类事物相比较时，它好或坏的程度
senses.example: The quality of the sound on that old tape is still remarkable.
senses.exampleCN: 那盘旧磁带的声音质量依然出色。
senses.why: Latin qualitas named the nature of a thing; judging that nature against other natures produced the modern sense of a standard.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 qualitas 本指事物的本性；把这种本性与别的本性相比较，就产生了现代「质量水准」的意思。

senses.title: A feature of a thing or person
senses.definition: a detail or feature that forms part of the nature of a person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 构成人或事物本性的一部分的具体细节或特征
senses.example: Hardness is one quality of diamond that makes it so useful.
senses.exampleCN: 坚硬是钻石如此有用的一项特性。
senses.why: If qualitas is the whole nature of a thing, then each part of that nature can be singled out and called a quality.
senses.whyCN: 如果 qualitas 指一物的整体本性，那么把这本性中的每一项单独拎出来，就可以称为一项 quality。

senses.title: A good personal trait
senses.definition: a part of someone's character that is good and worth praising
senses.definitionCN: 一个人性格中值得称赞的良性部分
senses.example: Honesty is the quality I value most in a friend.
senses.exampleCN: 诚实是我在朋友身上最看重的品质。
senses.why: English speakers narrowed the neutral word for nature to the traits people praise, so a quality often means a virtue.
senses.whyCN: 英语使用者把这个中性的「本性」一词收窄到人们称赞的性格特征，于是 a quality 常常就是一项美德。

senses.title: A high standard of excellence
senses.definition: a level of excellence clearly above the ordinary, often used before a noun
senses.definitionCN: 明显高于普通水准的优良程度，常放在名词前作定语
senses.example: This shop sells quality furniture at fair prices.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店以公道的价格出售优质家具。
senses.why: Once the word meant standard in general, shops could use it as a badge: goods of quality are goods of high standard.
senses.whyCN: 这个词既然泛指「水准」，商家就能把它当成品级标记来用：goods of quality 就是高水准的货物。

senses.title: The character of a sound
senses.definition: the particular character of a voice or an instrument as heard by the ear
senses.definitionCN: 人声或乐器被耳朵听到时所具有的独特性质
senses.example: The piano has a warm quality that fills the room.
senses.exampleCN: 这架钢琴有一种温暖、能充满房间的音色。
senses.why: The sense of nature extends to what the ear perceives, so the nature of a sound is also called its quality.
senses.whyCN: 「本性」这一层意思可以延伸到耳朵所感知的东西，所以一种声音的本性也被称作它的 quality。

intro.en: Quality goes back to the Latin question word for of what kind and to the noun coined from it; French carried the word to English, where it split into standard, feature and excellence.
intro.cn: quality 源自拉丁语中表示「何种」的疑问词以及由它造出的名词；法语把这个词带入英语，随后它分化为「水准、特征、优质」几层意思。

items.en: Qualis was the question word for of what kind, and it stood at the head of a family of words about the nature of things.
items.cn: qualis 是表示「何种」的疑问词，它站在一整族谈论事物本性的词的最前面。

items.en: Qualitas was coined to name the answer to that question: the whatness of a thing, its nature taken as a whole.
items.cn: qualitas 是为回答那个问题而造的名词：一物的「什么性」，把它的本性当作整体来看。

items.en: Old French took the noun as qualite and used it for the character or rank of a person or thing.
items.cn: 古法语把这个名词接受为 qualite，用来指人或事物的性质或等级。

items.en: Middle English used qualite for nature and rank, and later spelling was reshaped toward the Latin form as quality.
items.cn: 中古英语用 qualite 表示本性与等级，后来的拼写又被改造成接近拉丁语的 quality。

items.en: Modern English keeps the neutral sense of standard and adds the senses of a single feature, of personal virtue and of high grade.
items.cn: 现代英语保留了中性的「水准」义，又增加了单项特征、个人品德与高档品级这几层意思。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same Latin stem of kind; the near-meaning group gathers nouns for features, traits and grades.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁词干（何种）上的词；近义组收表示特征、品性与等级的名词。

entries.definition: A certificate or skill showing that a person meets a standard.
entries.definitionCN: 证明某人达到某项标准的证书或技能。

entries.definition: Based on qualities rather than on measured amounts.
entries.definitionCN: 依据性质而非测得数量的。

entries.definition: A match that decides who advances, or a word that limits another.
entries.definitionCN: 决定谁晋级的比赛，或限定另一词的词。

entries.definition: To meet a standard or to gain a right.
entries.definitionCN: 达到标准或取得某项权利。

entries.definition: A feature that belongs to a thing and affects how it behaves.
entries.definitionCN: 属于某物并影响其表现的特征。

entries.definition: A quality that is regarded as part of a person or thing.
entries.definitionCN: 被视为人或事物一部分的性质。

entries.definition: A feature that makes a person or thing easy to recognize.
entries.definitionCN: 使人或事物容易被辨认出来的特征。

entries.definition: A level of quality given to goods or work.
entries.definitionCN: 给货物或工作评定的质量等级。

normalIntro.en: The word answers the old question of what kind a thing is; from that answer English drew the ideas of standard, trait and high grade.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词回答的是古老的问题：一物属于哪一种；英语从这个答案里引出了水准、特征与高档这几层意思。

normal.en: Quality and qualify share the Latin question of what kind: to qualify is to prove which kind you are, and quality is the kind itself.
normal.cn: quality 与 qualify 共用拉丁语「何种」这一问：使合格就是证明你属于哪一类，而 quality 就是那个类别本身。

normal.en: The plural qualities is the usual word for the separate traits of one person's character.
normal.cn: 复数 qualities 常用来指一个人性格中一项项分开的特征。

normal.en: Qualitative work asks what kind something is, while quantitative work asks how much of it there is.
normal.cn: 定性工作问的是某物属于哪一类，定量工作问的则是它的量有多少。

normal.en: In shops, quality before a noun is a short badge for high grade, as in quality paper or quality service.
normal.cn: 在商店里，quality 放在名词前就是「高档」的简写标记，如优质纸张、优质服务。

normal.en: The quality of a sound is what the ear notices apart from its loudness: warm, sharp, flat or full.
normal.cn: 声音的 quality 是耳朵在音量之外察觉到的特点：温暖、尖利、平淡或饱满。

abstract.en: A quality is a judgment that never exists alone: it always compares one thing with another of its kind.
abstract.cn: 质量是一种从不单独存在的判断：它总要把一物与同类中的另一物相比。

abstract.en: The same word names what a thing is and how good it is, because in English the nature of a thing and its worth are hard to separate.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指某物是什么，又指它有多好，因为在英语里，一物的本性与它的价值很难分开。

abstract.en: To praise someone's qualities is to treat character as a set of parts that can be counted.
abstract.cn: 称赞某人的品质，就是把性格当作一组可以逐项清点的部分。

examples.en: The quality of the recording is poor, but the music is still worth hearing.
examples.cn: 录音质量很差，但这音乐仍然值得一听。

examples.en: Patience is a quality that grows only through practice.
examples.cn: 耐心是一种只能通过练习才能生长的品质。

examples.en: The hotel is known for quality service rather than for low prices.
examples.cn: 这家旅馆出名靠的是优质服务，而不是低价。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「夸了提」——东西好到大家夸了又提，说明质量过硬，记住 quality 是质量、品质。

root: 拉丁语 qualis（何种的）→ qualitas（本性、性质）→ 古法语 qualite → 英语 quality；同族有 qualify、qualification、qualitative。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the nature of a thing; the senses run from the whole nature to a single feature, then to a praised trait, to high grade and to the character of a sound.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一物的本性；义项从整体本性走向单项特征，再走向受称赞的品德、高档品级，最后走向声音的特质。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old plank rubbed smooth, its grain clear and its weight solid in the hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块被反复打磨的旧木板，纹理清晰，握在手里沉实。

branches.en: a ruler laid against two planks
branches.cn: 一把放在两块木板旁比较的尺

branches.en: one clear line of grain in the wood
branches.cn: 木料上一条清晰的纹理

branches.en: a friend who keeps a promise
branches.cn: 一个守信的朋友

branches.en: a shop window marked with a grade
branches.cn: 橱窗上标着品级的标签

branches.en: a warm note held in the ear
branches.cn: 一段留在耳边的温暖音符

intro.en: The word is held together by the Latin question word for kind, the suffix that turns it into a noun, and the English endings that build related adjectives and verbs.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语中询问种类的疑问词、把它变成名词的后缀，以及构成相关形容词与动词的英语词缀共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: Latin left a short but clear family around the question word for kind.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语围绕「何种」这个疑问词留下了一个短而清楚的同族词群。

definition_zh: 两个人依法律或习俗结成的夫妻关系，也指确立这种关系的婚礼
definition_en: the legally or socially recognized union of two people as spouses, and the ceremony that establishes it
core_image: 一张铺着红纸的桌上并排放着两只旧戒指、一份证书和一把新房钥匙
scene: 老屋的堂屋里点着两支红烛，墙上贴着一张写满吉利话的纸。 Her grandparents' marriage began with a ceremony that lasted three days.
sceneCN: 这里 marriage 指「两人依俗结成的夫妻结合」（第 1 个义项：由仪式与公认确立的配偶关系）；句意为她祖父母的婚姻始于一场持续三天的婚礼。可辨识物件：红烛、喜字、戒指、证书、钥匙；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: The recognized union of spouses
senses.titleCN: 被法律或社会承认的夫妻结合
senses.definition: the state in which two people are legally or socially recognized as spouses
senses.definitionCN: 两个人被法律或社会承认为配偶的状态
senses.example: Their marriage was registered at the county office in spring.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的婚姻是春天在县里登记的。
senses.why: from Latin maritus 'husband', the noun names the wedded state itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词来自拉丁 maritus「丈夫」，直接指已婚状态本身。

senses.title: The wedding ceremony itself
senses.definition: the event in which vows are exchanged and the union is publicly made
senses.definitionCN: 交换誓言并公开确立结合的那场活动
senses.example: The whole village came to the marriage and stayed for the feast.
senses.exampleCN: 全村人都来参加婚礼，并留下来吃喜宴。
senses.why: the event and the state share one word because the rite is what creates the relation.
senses.whyCN: 仪式与状态共用一个词，因为正是仪式造成了这层关系。

senses.title: The ongoing state of being wed
senses.definition: the daily condition of living as a married couple over many years
senses.definitionCN: 多年来作为夫妻共同生活的日常状态
senses.example: Thirty years of marriage had taught them how to argue without wounding.
senses.exampleCN: 三十年的婚姻教会他们如何争吵却不伤人。
senses.why: the noun covers duration, not only the moment of union.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词涵盖持续时间，而不只是结合的那一刻。

senses.title: A type of marriage system
senses.definition: a socially defined form such as monogamy or polygyny, studied as a rule of the group
senses.definitionCN: 如一夫一妻或一夫多妻这类被社会定义的制度，作为群体规则来研究
senses.example: The community practiced marriage between cross-cousins.
senses.exampleCN: 这个社群实行交叉表亲之间的婚姻。
senses.why: societies classify forms of union, and the same noun labels the type.
senses.whyCN: 社会会给结合形式分类，同一个名词也就用来指类型。

senses.title: A close alliance between things
senses.titleCN: 事物之间的紧密结合（比喻义）
senses.definition: a metaphor for two different elements joined so closely that neither keeps its old shape
senses.definitionCN: 比喻两种不同成分紧密结合，彼此都不再保持原样
senses.example: The album is a marriage of folk melody and electronic rhythm.
senses.exampleCN: 这张专辑是民歌曲调与电子节奏的结合。
senses.why: the metaphor keeps the core idea of two parties becoming one.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留了「两方成为一体」的核心意思。

senses.title: A card game of matching pairs
senses.definition: a card game in which players collect matching pairs, named after the paired union
senses.definitionCN: 玩家收集同名对子的一种纸牌游戏，因配对而成名
senses.example: The old men played marriage beside the stove all evening.
senses.exampleCN: 老人们整晚在炉边玩配对纸牌。
senses.why: the game is named for the matched pair, echoing the union sense.
senses.whyCN: 这种游戏因成对的牌而得名，与「结合」义呼应。

senses.title: A religious sacrament
senses.definition: the union regarded as a sacred vow rather than only a civil contract
senses.definitionCN: 被视为神圣誓约、而非仅是民事契约的结合
senses.example: The church treats marriage as a vow made before God.
senses.exampleCN: 教会把婚姻视为在神面前立下的誓约。
senses.why: religions read the union as sacred, adding a layer the law does not supply.
senses.whyCN: 宗教把这种结合读作神圣的，添加了法律不提供的一层。

senses.title: A political alliance between families
senses.definition: a union arranged to bind two families, courts or states rather than two individuals
senses.definitionCN: 为联结两个家族、宫廷或国家而非两个个人而安排的婚姻
senses.example: The treaty was sealed by a marriage between the two courts.
senses.exampleCN: 条约由两个宫廷之间的联姻加以巩固。
senses.why: kinship was once a diplomatic instrument, and the noun named that instrument.
senses.whyCN: 亲属关系曾是外交工具，这个词就指那件工具。

senses.title: The legal registration of the union
senses.titleCN: 婚姻的法律登记与效力
senses.definition: the recorded act that gives the union standing in courts and in inheritance law
senses.definitionCN: 使这种结合在法院与继承法中生效的登记行为
senses.example: Without registration, the marriage had no standing in court.
senses.exampleCN: 没有登记，这段婚姻在法庭上不具效力。
senses.why: modern states turn the relation into a recorded fact with legal consequences.
senses.whyCN: 现代国家把这种关系变成一项带有法律后果的登记事实。

intro.en: Marriage reaches English through Old French mariage from Latin maritare 'to wed', a verb built on maritus 'husband'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: marriage 经古法语 mariage 来自拉丁 maritare「使成婚」，该动词由 maritus「丈夫」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Maritus meant 'husband, married man', with the feminine marita 'wife'. Its deeper origin is uncertain: the link to mas 'male' is often proposed but not demonstrated.
items.cn: maritus 意为「丈夫、已婚男子」，阴性形式为 marita「妻子」。其更深来源不确定：把它与 mas「男性」联系起来是常见假说，但未获证实。

items.en: Maritare meant 'to wed, to give in marriage', and was also used of joining a vine to a supporting tree, an image of two lives bound together.
items.cn: maritare 意为「使成婚、嫁娶」，也用于把葡萄藤接到支撑的树上，暗含两条生命被绑在一起。

items.en: Old French mariage named both the wedded state and the wedding feast, and carried both senses into English in the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 mariage 同时指已婚状态与婚宴，并在十三世纪把这两个义项带入英语。

items.en: English marriage kept the double sense from the start, so the same word names the relation and the day that begins it.
items.cn: 英语 marriage 从一开始就保留双重含义，同一个词既指关系，也指开启关系的那一天。

items.en: Canon law made marriage one of the sacraments, while civil law made it a contract with property consequences; both uses shaped the modern word.
items.cn: 教会法把婚姻列为圣事之一，世俗法则把它变成带有财产后果的契约；两种用法共同塑造了现代词义。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): no convincing Latin derivation of maritus has been established, and the recorded first uses of the card-game sense are not fixed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：maritus 尚无令人信服的拉丁派生来源；纸牌游戏义的最早书证年代也不固定。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same Latin stock; group two holds near synonyms for the union or the event.
note.cn: 第一组是同出这一拉丁词干的词；第二组是表示结合或仪式的近义词。

entries.definition: To take as a spouse or to join two people as spouses; marriage is the resulting state or event.
entries.definitionCN: 指娶、嫁或为两人证婚；marriage 是由此形成的状态或事件。

entries.definition: Of or relating to marriage, used in legal and medical contexts rather than in everyday talk.
entries.definitionCN: 指与婚姻有关的形容词，多用于法律与医学语境，而非日常口语。

entries.definition: A formal or religious word for the married state, felt as more solemn than marriage.
entries.definitionCN: 指已婚状态正式或宗教性的说法，比 marriage 更显庄重。

entries.definition: An old borrowing of the same French word, later displaced by marriage; it survives only in historical writing.
entries.definitionCN: 同一法语词的古老借形，后来被 marriage 取代，只在历史文献中留存。

entries.definition: The ceremony and its celebration, without saying anything about the years that follow.
entries.definitionCN: 只指仪式及其庆祝，不涉及婚后的岁月。

entries.definition: A general word for two things becoming one, used of states, trade bodies and couples alike.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指两物合而为一，国家、工会与伴侣都可使用。

entries.definition: A formal, often journalistic word for a wedding, always plural and slightly ornamental.
entries.definitionCN: 指婚礼的正式用语，常见于报道，总是复数且略带修饰色彩。

entries.definition: A lasting arrangement between two people or firms; it makes no claim about vows or law.
entries.definitionCN: 指两人或两家公司之间的长期安排，不涉及誓言或法律。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real word partnerships and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: maritus meant husband, and -age turns the person into the state: the husband-state, then the union.
normal.cn: maritus 指丈夫，-age 把人变成状态：先是「丈夫的身份」，再是婚姻。

normal.en: The family runs marry, marriage, marital, premarital, extramarital and marriageable.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 marry、marriage、marital、premarital、extramarital 与 marriageable。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: arranged marriage, marriage vows, marriage license, marriage of convenience.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：包办婚姻、结婚誓言、结婚证书、权宜婚姻。

normal.en: The metaphor is alive in phrases like a marriage of flavours or a marriage of styles.
normal.cn: 比喻义仍活跃，如风味的结合、风格的结合。

normal.en: The card game sense survives in regional play and in dictionaries, not in general speech.
normal.cn: 纸牌义仍留在地方玩法与词典中，日常口语已不常用。

abstract.en: Picture two streams meeting and then sharing one bed.
abstract.cn: 想象两条溪流汇合后共用一条河床。

abstract.en: Picture a knot tied in public and carried privately for years.
abstract.cn: 想象一个当众打好的结，被私人携带多年。

abstract.en: Picture a vine grafted onto a tree so that both keep growing.
abstract.cn: 想象一根藤接到树上，两者都继续生长。

examples.en: The law recognizes a marriage only after both parties sign the register.
examples.cn: 法律只有在双方签署登记簿后才承认婚姻。

examples.en: Their marriage survived drought, debt and two long separations.
examples.cn: 他们的婚姻熬过了干旱、债务与两次长期分离。

examples.en: Critics called the novel a marriage of detective plot and family saga.
examples.cn: 评论家称这部小说是侦探情节与家族史诗的结合。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「marry（结婚）+ age（年龄）」——到了年纪就结婚

root: 拉丁 maritus「丈夫」（阴性 marita「妻子」）→ 动词 maritare「使成婚」→ 古法语 mariage → 英语 marriage。maritus 的更深来源不确定，与 mas「男性」的联系仅为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one bond: two people are joined, and the joining is then read as an event, a daily state, a social rule, a metaphor, a game, a sacrament, a treaty and a register entry.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿同一个结合展开：两个人被连在一起，这个结合再依次被读作事件、日常状态、社会制度、比喻、游戏、圣事、盟约与登记记录。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two rings set side by side on one sheet of paper, neither complete without the other.
core.cn: 核心意象：两枚戒指并排放在同一张纸上，缺一枚都不成双。

branches.en: THE BOND AND ITS RECORD: the relation comes first, and the register is how a state sees it.
branches.cn: 结合与记录：关系在先，登记则是国家看见它的方式。

branches.en: THE DAY AND THE VOW: a public rite turns a private promise into a recognised union.
branches.cn: 那一天与那誓言：公开仪式把私下承诺变成被承认的结合。

branches.en: THE LONG MIDDLE: most of a marriage is neither the wedding nor the law but ordinary duration.
branches.cn: 漫长的中间段：婚姻的大部分既不是婚礼也不是法律，而是平常的持续。

branches.en: RULES AND ALLIANCES: a group can define the form, and families can use it as a treaty.
branches.cn: 规则与联盟：群体可以规定形式，家族也可以把它当作条约。

branches.en: TWO BECOME ONE: the metaphor and the card game both play on the matched pair.
branches.cn: 合二为一：比喻义与纸牌义都借成对之物做文章。

intro.en: Marriage is a Latin noun stem plus a French ending, and the same stem builds the legal, medical and everyday words around it.
intro.cn: marriage 由一个拉丁名词词干加一个法语词尾构成，同一词干还构成它周围的法律、医学与日常用词。

latinIntro.en: Latin maritus and marita sit behind marriage, marry and marital; the ending -age names a state or a collection.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 maritus 与 marita 是 marriage、marry 与 marital 的来源；词尾 -age 表状态或集合。

items.example: Maritus supplied the whole family of words.
items.exampleCN: maritus 提供了整个词族的来源。

items.example: The feminine form fills out the pair.
items.exampleCN: 阴性形式补全了这一对。

items.structure: maritare, maritavi, maritatum (Latin verb, first conjugation)
items.example: The verb could also mean to join a vine to a tree.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词也可指把藤接到树上。

items.example: The suffix turns the act of wedding into a lasting state.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把成婚之举变成持续状态。

items.example: Old French kept both senses in one word.
items.exampleCN: 古法语用一个词保留了这两个义项。

items.example: English kept the double sense intact.
items.exampleCN: 英语完整保留了这双重含义。

items.example: Marry is the verb behind the noun.
items.exampleCN: marry 是名词背后的动词。

items.meaning: relating to a husband or to marriage
items.example: Marital law speaks of duties between spouses.
items.exampleCN: 婚姻法讲的是配偶之间的义务。

items.example: Premarital agreements are signed before the wedding.
items.exampleCN: 婚前协议在婚礼之前签署。

definition_zh: 承担；着手做；从事；承诺；答应负责
definition_en: to take on a task or responsibility and start doing it, or to promise formally that you will do something
core_image: 伸手把一件大事从架子上接下来，扛到自己肩上
scene: 新桥动工前，工程师在图纸上签下了自己的名字。 The chief engineer agreed to undertake the design of the new bridge.
sceneCN: 这里 undertake 是动词「承担、着手做」（第 1 个义项：接下任务并开始做）；句意为总工程师同意承担新桥的设计工作。

pos.zh: 承接任务；从事某项工作

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「事业；任务；（正式）承诺」
由本词加施动者后缀构成，义为「殡葬承办人」，为词义偏移的特殊用法

senses.title: To take on and start a task
senses.definition: to accept a task or duty and begin working on it
senses.definitionCN: 接受任务或职责并着手开始做
senses.example: The lab will undertake a three-year study of sleep patterns.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室将开展一项为期三年的睡眠模式研究。
senses.why: Under plus stand puts you beneath the work: once you take it on, the weight rests on your shoulders and you must stand up under it.
senses.whyCN: under 加 stand 把你置于工作之下：一旦接下，重量便落在肩头，你必须扛着它站起来。

senses.title: To promise formally
senses.definition: to state formally that you will do something, often in writing or speech
senses.definitionCN: 正式表示将做某事，常以书面或口头形式作出
senses.example: The company undertook to refund every customer within thirty days.
senses.exampleCN: 该公司承诺在三十天内向每位客户退款。
senses.why: Taking on a duty in words is like taking on the work itself: the promise puts the load on you before any real work starts.
senses.whyCN: 用言语接下职责如同接下工作本身：承诺在任何实际工作开始之前就把担子压在你身上。

senses.title: To accept responsibility or obligation
senses.definition: to accept that you are responsible for something, such as a duty, debt, or duty of care
senses.definitionCN: 接受对某事的负责，如职责、债务或注意义务
senses.example: By signing the lease, she undertook responsibility for repairs to the roof.
senses.exampleCN: 签下租约后，她承担起修缮屋顶的责任。
senses.why: Standing under a beam means accepting everything that falls on it; accepting responsibility is agreeing to be that beam.
senses.whyCN: 立于梁下意味着承受一切落在梁上的东西；接受责任就是同意成为那根梁。

senses.title: To engage in an activity
senses.definition: to carry out an activity or course of action, especially a formal or planned one
senses.definitionCN: 进行某项活动或行动方案，尤指正式或有计划的工作
senses.example: The army undertook a review of its training procedures.
senses.exampleCN: 军方对其训练流程进行了一次审查。
senses.why: The compound treats the activity as a standing position: you are under it, and doing it is simply holding that position until it is done.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词把活动当作一种站立的姿态：你在它之下，做它就是保持那个姿态直到完成。

senses.title: To accept a risk or burden
senses.definition: to accept the risks, costs, or burdens that come with an action
senses.definitionCN: 接受某一行动所带来的风险、成本或负担
senses.example: Every climber who signs up undertakes the risks of high altitude.
senses.exampleCN: 每位报名的登山者都接受高海拔带来的风险。
senses.why: To be under something is to be exposed to its weight; undertaking a risk is letting that weight stand over you by choice.
senses.whyCN: 在某种东西之下就是暴露于它的重量之中；接受风险就是自愿让那重量悬在自己上方。

senses.title: A journey or venture begun
senses.titleCN: 启程 undertaking：一项已启程的事业
senses.definition: in older or literary use, to set out on a journey or an enterprise
senses.definitionCN: 旧式或文学用法，指开始一段旅程或一项事业
senses.example: They undertook the crossing of the desert at first light.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在天刚亮时踏上穿越沙漠的旅程。
senses.why: A journey undertaken is a burden lifted and carried forward; the word keeps this older image of setting out with a load.
senses.whyCN: 被承担的旅程是被举起并向前背负的担子；这个词保留了「负重启程」的旧意象。

senses.title: To pledge in law or contract
senses.titleCN: 在法律或合同中作出承诺
senses.definition: to give a formal, often binding, assurance, as in an undertaking given to a court
senses.definitionCN: 作出正式且有约束力的保证，如向法院出具的承诺
senses.example: Counsel undertook to hand over the documents by Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 律师承诺在周五前移交文件。
senses.why: A legal undertaking is the promise sense fixed in place: standing under the words means they can be enforced against you.
senses.whyCN: 法律上的承诺把「承诺」义项固定下来：立于言辞之下，意味着这些言辞可以对你产生强制力。

senses.title: To take on the management of something
senses.definition: to take charge of arranging or managing something, such as an event or funeral
senses.definitionCN: 负责安排或操办某事，如一场活动或葬礼
senses.example: The school undertook the organization of the whole festival.
senses.exampleCN: 学校承担了整个节日活动的组织工作。
senses.why: Managing is standing beneath the moving parts so they do not fall; the one who holds things up is the one who has undertaken.
senses.whyCN: 管理就是站在各运转部件之下托住它们不让其坠落；托住一切的人正是承担了它的人。

intro.en: Undertake is a pure Old English compound: under plus take, a hand reaching beneath a load to lift it onto the back.
intro.cn: undertake 是纯粹的古英语复合词：under 加 take，像一只手伸到重物之下把它举上背。

items.en: *n̥dher- is reconstructed as 'below, under'; *deh₃- is generally reconstructed as 'to give', the source of take's Germanic ancestor. The deeper origins remain source uncertain.
items.cn: 原始印欧语重构形式 *n̥dher- 表示「在下」；*deh₃- 一般认为表示「给予」，是 take 日耳曼语祖先的来源；更深的来源不确定。

items.en: Old English undertacan meant to take on oneself, to receive, or to catch hold from beneath.
items.cn: 古英语 undertacan 意为「承当于己；接受；从下方抓住」。

items.en: By the thirteenth and fourteenth centuries the verb meant to take upon oneself a duty, a journey, or a venture.
items.cn: 十三至十四世纪时，该动词已表示承担职责、旅程或事业于己身。

items.en: The sense narrowed toward beginning a task and promising to do it; Shakespeare uses undertake for taking charge of an enterprise.
items.cn: 词义逐渐收窄为「着手做某事」与「承诺去做」；莎士比亚即用 undertake 表示接手一项事业。

items.en: One who undertakes any task came, by euphemism in the seventeenth to eighteenth centuries, to name the one who undertakes the dead: the undertaker.
items.cn: 十七至十八世纪间，通过委婉用法，「承接任何事务的人」转而专指「承办丧事的人」：undertaker。

items.en: Today the verb lives in formal registers: projects are undertaken, promises are undertaken, obligations are undertaken.
items.cn: 如今该动词多用于正式语域：项目被承担，承诺被作出，义务被肩负。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the under- compound family; the near-meaning group gathers words for taking on duties and beginning work.
note.cn: 形近组收 under- 复合词族；近义组收承担职责与着手工作类词。

entries.definition: The noun for a task, venture, or formal promise.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「事业；任务；（正式）承诺」。

entries.definition: Under plus stand; a sibling compound, but about the mind rather than the hand.
entries.definitionCN: under 加 stand 的姊妹复合词，义为「理解」，关乎心智而非双手。

entries.definition: To experience or endure; the sibling that receives rather than takes.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「经历；承受」，是承接而非主动去拿的姊妹词。

entries.definition: Under one's feet; an adverb compound of the same under- family.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「在脚下」，同一 under- 词族的副词性复合词。

entries.definition: A quiet or hidden tone beneath the surface of a voice or colour.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「低调；底色」，指声音或色彩表面之下的暗层。

entries.definition: To take on a duty or role, often without being asked.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「承担；就任」，多指主动承接职责或角色。

entries.definition: To bear a burden on your shoulders; vivid and physical.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「肩负」，形象化地表达负重。

entries.definition: To begin a long or important venture; stresses the start.
entries.definitionCN: 短语动词，义为「着手；开始」，强调重大事业的起点。

entries.definition: To bind yourself to a course of action; stresses firmness.
entries.definitionCN: 短语动词，义为「承诺投入」，强调坚定不移。

entries.definition: To accept work or responsibility; the everyday, lighter counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 短语动词，义为「承担；接手」，是更日常的说法。

normalIntro.en: Five anchors from the word's own structure and family.
normalIntro.cn: 五个来自词形结构与词族的记忆锚点。

normal.en: Under plus take: reach beneath the load and take it onto your back.
normal.cn: under 加 take：伸手到重物之下，把它接到背上。

normal.en: Undertook, undertaken follow the irregular pattern of take, took, taken.
normal.cn: undertook、undertaken 遵循 take→took→taken 的不规则变化模式。

normal.en: An undertaking is both the work you take on and the promise you make.
normal.cn: undertaking 既指你接下的工作，也指你许下的承诺。

normal.en: Understand and undergo are siblings: stand under, go under, take under.
normal.cn: understand 与 undergo 是同族：立于其下、行于其下、接于其下。

normal.en: The undertaker is the one who undertakes the last task of all.
normal.cn: undertaker 是承接最后一项事务的人——殡葬承办人。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge beam resting on your shoulders as you sign your name beneath it.
abstract.cn: 想象桥的横梁压在肩上，你在梁下签下自己的名字。

abstract.en: Signing is undertaking: the ink dries and the weight is yours.
abstract.cn: 签名即承担：墨迹一干，重量便归你所有。

abstract.en: To undertake is to become the beam that others can build on.
abstract.cn: 承担就是成为一根可供他人搭建的梁。

examples.en: The charity undertook to rebuild every damaged school within two years.
examples.cn: 该慈善机构承诺在两年内重建所有受损的学校。

examples.en: She undertook a careful revision of the entire manuscript.
examples.cn: 她对整部手稿进行了一次细致的修订。

examples.en: Who will undertake the responsibility if the project fails?
examples.cn: 如果项目失败，谁来承担责任？

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安德忒克」——安（安德）在下面（under）特意（忒）接着（take）：在下面接住重物，即承担

root: 古英语 undertacan「承当于己；从下方抓住」，由 under「在下」加 tacan「抓住、拿取」复合而成；under 溯至原始印欧语重构形式 *n̥dher-「在下」，take 的日耳曼语祖先一般溯至 *deh₃-「给予」（经北欧语传入英语，来源细节存疑）；字面意象「在下接取」一直支撑着「承担」义。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses of undertake all begin with one gesture: reaching beneath a load to take it up — a task, a promise, a risk, a responsibility, or a whole venture.
sensesIntro.cn: undertake 的八个义项都始于同一个动作：伸手到重物之下把它接起来——可以是任务、承诺、风险、职责，或整项事业。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand reaching under a load and taking it onto the back
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手伸到重物之下，把它接到背上

branches.en: THE WORK: tasks and activities taken up and carried through.
branches.cn: 工作线：被接起并完成到底的任务与活动。

branches.en: THE WORD: promises and legal pledges that fix the load in place.
branches.cn: 言辞线：把担子固定下来的承诺与法律保证。

branches.en: THE DUTY: responsibility accepted like a beam across the shoulders.
branches.cn: 职责线：如横梁压肩般被接受的责任。

branches.en: THE ROAD: risks accepted and journeys begun under one's own weight.
branches.cn: 道路线：被接受的风险与自行背负启程的旅程。

branches.en: THE HANDOVER: taking charge so nothing falls while it is being arranged.
branches.cn: 操办线：接手管理，让一切在安排过程中不致坠落。

intro.en: Undertake is built from two native Old English words, each still living in English.
intro.cn: undertake 由两个古英语本族词构成，二者至今仍在英语中使用。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic, not Latin, so there are no Latin cognates to list; the deep roots are reconstructions.
latinIntro.cn: 该词属日耳曼语源而非拉丁语源，故没有拉丁同族词可列；深层词根属重构形式。

definition_zh: 器官；管风琴；机构；喉舌；工具
definition_en: a part of a living body that performs a special function, or an instrument, body or publication that serves a particular purpose
core_image: 一台有专门职责的装置，嵌在更大的机器里，各自完成一道工序
scene: 医院走廊的指示牌上画着人体轮廓，每个部位旁标注它负责的功能： Each organ in the abdomen has its own job.
sceneCN: 这里指「生物器官」（第 1 个义项：执行特定功能的独立身体部件）；句意为腹腔里的每个器官都有各自的分工；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 器官（身体中执行特定功能的部分）
管风琴；机构；机关报刊；喉舌

senses.title: Body organ
senses.titleCN: 生物器官：执行特定功能的部件
senses.definition: a part of an animal or plant body made of several tissues and carrying out a special job
senses.definitionCN: 由多种组织构成、承担特定功能的动物或植物身体部件
senses.example: Each organ in the abdomen has its own job.
senses.exampleCN: 腹腔里的每个器官都有自己的职责。
senses.why: The oldest anatomical sense treats the body as a machine with distinct working parts, each named for its task.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的解剖义把身体当作一台有明确工作部件的机器，每个部件按任务命名。

senses.title: Pipe organ
senses.titleCN: 管风琴：由多组音管构成的乐器
senses.definition: a large musical instrument in which air is forced through pipes to produce sound
senses.definitionCN: 让气流通过音管发声的大型乐器
senses.example: The cathedral organ filled the hall with sound.
senses.exampleCN: 教堂的管风琴让整个大厅充满声音。
senses.why: The instrument is a set of pipes each doing one job, so the body-part word was applied to a machine made of specialised parts.
senses.whyCN: 这件乐器是一组各司其职的音管，于是「身体部件」这个词被用到由专门部件构成的机器上。

senses.title: Government body
senses.definition: an official institution that carries out a particular public function
senses.definitionCN: 承担某项公共职能的官方机构
senses.example: The central bank is an organ of the state, not a private company.
senses.exampleCN: 中央银行是国家机关，不是私人公司。
senses.why: An institution is a working part of the state in the same way an organ is a working part of a body.
senses.whyCN: 机构是国家的执行部件，正如器官是身体的执行部件。

senses.title: Party newspaper
senses.definition: a newspaper or magazine that speaks officially for a party, union or movement
senses.definitionCN: 代表政党、工会或运动正式发声的报纸或杂志
senses.example: The party's official organ published the speech in full.
senses.exampleCN: 该党的机关报全文刊登了这篇讲话。
senses.why: A publication becomes the mouth of an organization, so the body-part word shifts from doing work to speaking for the whole.
senses.whyCN: 出版物成为组织的嘴，于是这个身体部件词从「执行工作」转为「替整体发声」。

senses.title: Vocal organs
senses.definition: the parts of the body, such as the larynx and vocal cords, used to produce voice
senses.definitionCN: 喉、声带等用于产生声音的身体部件
senses.example: Damage to the vocal organs can change a singer's range.
senses.exampleCN: 发声器官受损会改变歌手的音域。
senses.why: Speech is a bodily function, so the parts that produce it are organs in the strict anatomical sense.
senses.whyCN: 言语是一种身体功能，产生它的部件按严格解剖义就是器官。

senses.title: Sense organ
senses.definition: a structure such as the eye or ear that receives a particular kind of stimulus
senses.definitionCN: 眼、耳等接收特定刺激的结构
senses.example: The eye is a sense organ tuned to light.
senses.exampleCN: 眼睛是对光敏感的感觉器官。
senses.why: Each sense has a dedicated receiver, and a dedicated working part is exactly what the word organ names.
senses.whyCN: 每种感觉都有专门的接收器，而「专门的执行部件」正是这个词所指。

senses.title: Reproductive organ
senses.definition: a structure that produces or carries sex cells, such as the flower of a plant
senses.definitionCN: 产生或承载生殖细胞的结构，如植物的花
senses.example: The flower is the reproductive organ of the plant.
senses.exampleCN: 花是植物的繁殖器官。
senses.why: The botanical use extends the anatomical word to plants, where a flower is the dedicated part for one function.
senses.whyCN: 植物学把这个解剖词扩展到植物：花就是专司一项功能的部件。

senses.title: Instrument or means, archaic
senses.definition: an instrument or means by which something is done, the oldest general sense of the word
senses.definitionCN: 用来做某事的工具或手段，是该词最古老的泛义
senses.example: In old texts, a pen is called the organ of the writer.
senses.exampleCN: 在古老文本里，笔被称为书写者的工具。
senses.why: Greek organon meant any tool, so English once used organ for instruments in general before the body and music senses took over.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语这个词泛指任何工具，因此英语早期曾用它泛指器具，后来才被身体义与音乐义占据。

intro.en: Organ comes from Latin organum, borrowed from Greek organon, a tool or instrument, which is generally connected with Greek ergon work. The musical and bodily senses developed separately. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: organ 来自拉丁 organum，借自希腊 organon「工具、器具」，一般认为与希腊 ergon「工作」有关。音乐义与身体义各自独立发展。年代均为约数。

items.en: Greek organon meant a tool, implement or instrument, including a musical instrument and, in medical writing, a part of the body.
items.cn: 希腊 organon 意为工具、器具或乐器，在医学写作中也指身体的一部分。

items.en: The usual account connects organon with ergon work, so a tool is what does work; the Indo-European root behind ergon is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 通行解释把 organon 与 ergon「工作」联系起来，即工具就是干活的东西；ergon 背后的印欧词根属重构形式。

items.en: Latin borrowed organum for an instrument, engine or musical instrument, and used it in translations of Greek medical texts.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入 organum，指器具、器械或乐器，并在翻译希腊医学文献时使用它。

items.en: The church organ gave the word its everyday musical sense in medieval English, where organ meant the instrument before it meant the body part.
items.cn: 教堂管风琴让这个词在中古英语中获得日常音乐义：在指身体部件之前，organ 先指这件乐器。

items.en: The body sense was revived through medical Latin in the sixteenth century and then spread to every part with a special function.
items.cn: 身体义在 16 世纪经医学拉丁语重新兴起，随后扩展到每一个有专门功能的部件。

items.en: The sense of an official body or newspaper developed from the older idea of an instrument or mouthpiece; the exact dates of each branch are uncertain.
items.cn: 官方机构或机关报的义项由更早的「工具、喉舌」观念发展而来；各支线确切的年代存疑。

note.en: The first group holds forms built on organ; the second holds body parts and general words that are often swapped for it.
note.cn: 第一组是由 organ 构成的同根形式；第二组是常与它替换的身体部件词与泛用词。

entries.definition: A specialised structure inside a cell; the suffix -elle makes it a little organ, smaller than an organ.
entries.definitionCN: 细胞内的专门结构；后缀 -elle 使它成为「小器官」，比器官更小。

entries.definition: A whole living being, not one of its parts; the suffix -ism marks the total body.
entries.definitionCN: 完整的活体，而非其中一个部件；后缀 -ism 标记整体。

entries.definition: Relating to organs or to living things; it describes and cannot stand for the noun organ.
entries.definitionCN: 与器官或生物有关的；它是描述词，不能代替名词 organ。

entries.definition: The Latin noun behind organ, still used in historical music writing for early polyphony.
entries.definitionCN: organ 背后的拉丁名词，在音乐史写作中仍指早期复调。

entries.definition: A layer of similar cells; organs are built from several tissues, so tissue is the material and organ the working unit.
entries.definitionCN: 相似细胞构成的一层；器官由多种组织建成，因此组织是材料，器官是工作单位。

entries.definition: An organ that makes and releases a substance; it is one kind of organ, not a synonym for all organs.
entries.definitionCN: 制造并释放物质的器官；它是器官的一种，并非所有器官的同义词。

entries.definition: An arm, leg or wing; a limb is an appendage, while an organ is an internal working part.
entries.definitionCN: 臂、腿或翼；肢体是附肢，而器官是内部执行部件。

entries.definition: Any tool or means, including a musical instrument; it overlaps the oldest sense of organ but lacks the body sense.
entries.definitionCN: 任何工具或手段，包括乐器；它与 organ 最古老的义项重叠，但没有身体义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Greek tool-word, the real musical history and the real anatomical family.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊工具词、真实的音乐史与真实的解剖词族。

normal.en: Greek organon meant tool; a body organ is the tool a body uses for a job.
normal.cn: 希腊 organon 意为工具；身体器官就是身体干活用的工具。

normal.en: The musical sense came first in English: organ meant the church instrument before it meant the body part.
normal.cn: 音乐义在英语中先出现：organ 先指教堂乐器，后指身体部件。

normal.en: Organelle is a little organ inside a cell; the suffix -elle marks the smaller scale.
normal.cn: organelle 是细胞里的小器官；后缀 -elle 标记更小的尺度。

normal.en: Official organ is the fixed phrase for a party newspaper, keeping the mouthpiece image.
normal.cn: official organ 是机关报的固定说法，保留了「喉舌」的意象。

normal.en: Vital organs, sense organs and reproductive organs name the function each set performs.
normal.cn: vital organs、sense organs、reproductive organs 都按各自执行的功能命名。

abstract.en: Picture a workshop where every bench has one job and no bench does another's work.
abstract.cn: 想象一间作坊，每张工作台只做一道工序，绝不替别人干活。

abstract.en: Picture a pipe organ: many pipes, one instrument, each pipe responsible for one note.
abstract.cn: 想象一架管风琴：许多音管，一件乐器，每根管负责一个音。

abstract.en: Picture a newspaper as a mouth: the institution speaks through it the way a body speaks through a throat.
abstract.cn: 想象报纸是一张嘴：机构通过它发声，正如身体通过喉咙发声。

examples.en: The liver is an organ that removes toxins from the blood.
examples.cn: 肝脏是从血液中清除毒素的器官。

examples.en: The organ in the church was built in the eighteenth century.
examples.cn: 教堂里的管风琴建于 18 世纪。

examples.en: The committee is an organ of the local government.
examples.cn: 该委员会是地方政府的一个机关。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦，干」（organ）——哦，干活（干）的就是器官与机构 → 器官；机构

root: 拉丁 organum，借自希腊 organon「工具、器具、乐器」，一般认为与 ergon「工作」相关；ergon 的印欧祖形为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all name a part with a job: a body organ, a pipe organ, a state body, a party paper, vocal organs, sense organs, plant reproductive organs, and finally any instrument at all.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都指「有专门职责的部件」：身体器官、管风琴、国家机关、机关报、发声器官、感觉器官、植物繁殖器官，最后泛指任何工具。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dedicated unit inside a larger machine, each unit doing one job.
core.cn: 核心意象：更大机器中的一个专职单元，每个单元只做一件事。

branches.en: BODY PARTS: voice, sense and reproductive parts each serve one function.
branches.cn: 身体部件：发声、感觉与繁殖部件各司一职。

branches.en: INSTRUMENT: a set of pipes, each with one job, becomes one musical organ.
branches.cn: 乐器：一组各司其职的音管，合成一件管风琴。

branches.en: PARTY VOICE: a newspaper speaks for a movement.
branches.cn: 党的喉舌：一份报纸替一场运动发声。

branches.en: THE OLD GENERAL SENSE: any tool or means, before the body and music senses narrowed the word.
branches.cn: 古老的泛义：在身体义与音乐义收窄词义之前，泛指任何工具或手段。

branches.en: ONE METAPHOR, TWO DOMAINS: body and state are both read as machines of specialised parts.
branches.cn: 一个比喻两个领域：身体与国家都被读作由专门部件组成的机器。

intro.en: Organ is a Greek loan that entered Latin, so its family mixes Greek suffixes with Latin and modern scientific endings.
intro.cn: organ 是经拉丁语进入的希腊借词，因此其词族混合了希腊后缀、拉丁后缀与现代科学词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin organum and Greek organikos give organic; Late Latin organizare gives organize and organization; New Latin organismus gives organism.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 organum 与希腊 organikos 衍生 organic；晚期拉丁 organizare 衍生 organize 与 organization；新拉丁 organismus 衍生 organism。

items.example: The Greek word named any instrument, including a musical one.
items.exampleCN: 这个希腊词泛指任何器具，包括乐器。

items.example: Latin medical texts used organum for body parts.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁医学文献用 organum 指身体部件。

items.structure: organum, shortened in French and English
items.example: Each organ in the abdomen has its own job.
items.exampleCN: 腹腔里的每个器官各有分工。

items.meaning: relating to organs or living things
items.example: Organic matter comes from living things.
A single cell can be a whole organism.
items.exampleCN: 单个细胞也可以是一个完整生物体。

items.meaningCN: 组织起来的机构或安排
items.example: The organization has offices in three cities.
items.exampleCN: 这个机构在三座城市设有办事处。

items.meaning: a small specialised part of a cell
items.meaningCN: 细胞内的小型专门结构

items.meaning: a person who plays the organ
items.example: The organist practised before the service.
items.exampleCN: 管风琴师在礼拜前练习。

items.meaning: a person who gives an organ for transplant
items.example: The register lists people willing to be an organ donor.
items.exampleCN: 登记册列出愿意捐献器官的人。

definition_zh: 根本的；彻底的；激进的；激进分子；根式
definition_en: relating to the root of a matter and therefore thorough; wanting great political or social change; a person who wants such change; a root expression in mathematics
core_image: 一棵被连根拔起的树，根须上还挂着泥土
scene: 会议室里，有人把一份厚厚的改革方案摊开，主张从制度本身动手。 The committee proposed radical changes to the way the city collects waste.
sceneCN: 这里 radical 是「根本的、彻底的」（第 1 个义项：触及事物根基因而彻底的）；句意为委员会提议对城市收运垃圾的方式进行彻底改革。画面里可留意：摊开的厚方案、被翻到卷边的页角。

pos.zh: 根本的；彻底的；激进的；根生的
激进分子；（数学）根式；（语言）词根

derivatives.zh: radical 加 -ly，指从根本上、彻底地
radical 加 -ism，指主张彻底变革的激进主义
radical 加 -ize，指使某人变得激进

senses.title: Relating to the root of a matter
senses.definition: touching the root or foundation of a problem, and therefore thorough
senses.definitionCN: 触及问题的根源或基础，因而十分彻底
senses.example: The plan calls for radical changes in the tax system.
senses.exampleCN: 这项计划要求对税制进行彻底改革。
senses.why: Latin radix meant a root, and radicalis meant belonging to a root, so a radical change goes down to the root of a thing.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 radix 意为根，radicalis 意为属于根的，因此 radical change 就是深入到事物根部的改变。

senses.title: Wanting great political change
senses.definition: favouring far-reaching change in politics or society, often by rapid means
senses.definitionCN: 主张在政治或社会上进行影响深远的改变，常指以较快手段实现
senses.example: The party's radical wing wants to abolish the old rules.
senses.exampleCN: 该党的激进派想废除旧规则。
senses.why: A reformer who wants to reach the root of a social problem is called radical, because the root is exactly what the word names.
senses.whyCN: 想触及社会问题根源的改革者被称为 radical，因为这个词命名的正是「根」。

senses.title: A person who wants such change
senses.definition: someone who holds radical political views and works for them
senses.definitionCN: 持激进政治观点并为之行动的人
senses.example: He was a radical in his youth and a moderate later.
senses.exampleCN: 他年轻时是激进分子，后来成了温和派。
senses.why: The adjective became a noun for the person who carries the quality, a common path in English.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词转化为名词，用来指具有这种性质的人，这是英语里常见的路径。

senses.title: Growing from the root
senses.definition: growing from or near the root of a plant, as some leaves do
senses.definitionCN: 从植物根部或近根部生长，如某些叶子
senses.example: Radical leaves of this plant lie almost flat on the ground.
senses.exampleCN: 这种植物的根生叶几乎平贴在地面上。
senses.why: Botany kept the plain Latin sense: a part attached at the root is literally radical.
senses.whyCN: 植物学保留了拉丁语最朴素的意思：附着在根部的部分字面上就是 radical。

senses.title: A root expression in mathematics
senses.definition: a mathematical expression written with a root sign, or the sign itself
senses.definitionCN: 用根号写成的数学表达式，或根号本身
senses.example: Simplify the radical before you add the two terms.
senses.exampleCN: 先把根式化简，再把两项相加。
senses.why: Mathematics uses the root image directly: the radical sign points to the root of a number.
senses.whyCN: 数学直接使用「根」这一意象：根号所指的就是一个数的根。

intro.en: Radical comes from the Latin word for root and its adjective, and the sense of thoroughness grew from the picture of reaching down to the root.
intro.cn: radical 源自拉丁语表示根的名词及其形容词，而「彻底」这一层意思从「向下触及根部」的画面生长出来。

items.en: Radix meant the root of a plant and, figuratively, the base or origin of anything.
items.cn: radix 指植物的根，也比喻任何事物的基础或起源。

items.en: The genitive radicis, of a root, supplied the stem from which the adjective was formed.
items.cn: 属格 radicis（根的）提供了构成形容词的词干。

items.en: Radicalis meant belonging to a root, and it was used in grammar and medicine as well as in botany.
items.cn: radicalis 意为属于根的，除植物学外也用于语法与医学。

items.en: English took the word for what goes to the root of a matter, and politics gave it the sense of far-reaching change.
items.cn: 英语接受这个词，用来指触及事物根本的东西，政治又赋予它「影响深远之变革」的意思。

items.en: Modern English keeps the senses of root cause, political extreme, root growth and the root sign in algebra.
items.cn: 现代英语保留了根本原因、政治上的极端、根部生长，以及代数中的根号这几层意思。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the Latin stem of root; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives of depth and extremes.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁语「根」词干上的词；近义组收表示深入与极端的形容词。

entries.definition: A small red root vegetable eaten raw.
entries.definitionCN: 一种生食的小红根菜。

entries.definition: To remove something completely, as if by pulling it out by the root.
entries.definitionCN: 像连根拔起那样彻底清除某物。

entries.definition: In a thorough or fundamental way.
entries.definitionCN: 以彻底或根本的方式。

entries.definition: The belief in far-reaching change.
entries.definitionCN: 主张彻底变革的信念。

entries.definition: Forming the base of something.
entries.definitionCN: 构成某物基础的。

entries.definition: Extreme and severe in effect.
entries.definitionCN: 作用极端而严厉的。

entries.definition: Far beyond the ordinary.
entries.definitionCN: 远远超出寻常的。

entries.definition: Complete in every detail.
entries.definitionCN: 每个细节都完备的。

normalIntro.en: The root is the picture: a change that goes to the root, a plant part at the root, and the root sign in algebra.
normalIntro.cn: 「根」就是这幅画面的核心：深入根部的改变、长在根部的植物部分，以及代数里的根号。

normal.en: Radical, radish and eradicate all share the Latin word for root, which makes the family easy to hold together.
normal.cn: radical、radish 与 eradicate 都共用拉丁语「根」一词，整族词因此很容易串在一起。

normal.en: A radical reform is not just a big reform; it is one that reaches the root of the system.
normal.cn: radical reform 不只是大改革，而是触及制度根基的改革。

normal.en: The radical sign in mathematics is shaped like a roof over a number, pointing back to its root.
normal.cn: 数学里的根号形状像一个盖在数字上的屋顶，指向它的根。

normal.en: Radical leaves grow at the base of the plant, which is the literal botanical sense.
normal.cn: radical leaves 长在植物基部，这正是植物学里的字面义。

normal.en: Radicalism is the noun for the belief, radicalize the verb for making someone hold it.
normal.cn: radicalism 是表示这种主张的名词，radicalize 是使某人接受它的动词。

abstract.en: To change something radically is to admit that the visible problem was only a symptom.
abstract.cn: 彻底改变某物，就是承认看得见的问题只是症状。

abstract.en: The same word can mean wise depth or dangerous haste, depending on who is describing the change.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既可指有智慧的深刻，也可指危险的急躁，取决于谁在描述这场改变。

abstract.en: Everything grows from a root, so the word for root quietly honors what is usually invisible.
abstract.cn: 万物都从根部长出，因此「根」这个词也在悄悄致敬那些通常看不见的部分。

examples.en: The company needs radical changes, not small adjustments.
examples.cn: 这家公司需要彻底变革，而不是小修小补。

examples.en: His radical views made him unpopular with the board.
examples.cn: 他的激进观点使他不受董事会欢迎。

examples.en: In algebra, we first simplify the radical and then solve the equation.
examples.cn: 在代数里，我们先化简根式，再解方程。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「锐的抠」——锐利地往根里抠，一直挖到最根本处，记住 radical 是根本的、激进的。

root: 拉丁语 radix（根）→ radicis（根的）→ 晚期拉丁语 radicalis（属于根的）→ 英语 radical；同族有 radish、eradicate、radically。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a root; the senses divide into a root-deep change, a political extreme, the person holding it, growth at the root and the root sign.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「根」；义项分为深入根源的改变、政治上的极端、持此立场的人、根部的生长，以及根号。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tree pulled up by its roots, earth still clinging to them.
core.cn: 核心意象：一棵被连根拔起的树，根须上还挂着泥土。

branches.en: a knife cutting down to the base
branches.cn: 一直切到根基的一刀

branches.en: a speaker demanding a new order
branches.cn: 要求建立新秩序的发言者

branches.en: leaves lying flat at the stem base
branches.cn: 平贴茎基部的叶子

branches.en: a sign drawn over a number
branches.cn: 画在数字上方的符号

branches.en: the same depth, once in a repair and once in politics
branches.cn: 同一种深入，一次在修补中，一次在政治中

intro.en: The word is built from the Latin noun for root, its stem and adjective ending, with English endings for adverbs, beliefs and verbs.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语表示根的名词、其词干与形容词词尾构成，再加上表示副词、主张与动词的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: The Latin stem radic- is short but reaches English in several common words.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词干 radic- 很短，却在英语里伸进了好几个常用词。

definition_zh: 计算；估计；打算
definition_en: to work out an amount or result using numbers
core_image: 在纸上一步步列出数字并相加
scene: 结账前他对着账单核对。 He calculated the total cost carefully.
sceneCN: 这里 calculate 是「计算」（第 1 个义项：用数字算出结果）；句意是他仔细计算了总花费。

derivatives.zh: 计算，由动词加 -ion 构成
计算器，由动词加 -or 构成

senses.title: To work out with numbers
senses.definition: to find a total or amount by using numbers
senses.definitionCN: 通过运算求出总数或数量
senses.example: He calculated the total cost carefully.
senses.exampleCN: 他仔细计算了总花费。
senses.why: The core image is small stones moved one by one to keep a count.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是一颗颗小石子被挪动，用来记数。

senses.title: To estimate or judge
senses.definition: to judge the likely amount or effect without exact figures
senses.definitionCN: 在没有精确数字时判断大致数量或效果
senses.example: We calculated that the trip would take three hours.
senses.exampleCN: 我们估计这趟行程要三个小时。
senses.why: Counting grew into judging, even when no exact sum is possible.
senses.whyCN: 从精确计数扩展到判断，即使算不出精确结果也用它。

senses.title: To intend for a purpose
senses.definition: to design something to have a particular effect
senses.definitionCN: 使某事物产生特定效果，用意在于
senses.example: The remark was calculated to calm the crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 那句话意在安抚人群。
senses.why: A planned effect is worked out in advance, like a sum on paper.
senses.whyCN: 预想的效果提前算好，就像纸上先列出的算式。

intro.en: Calculate comes from the Latin word for a counting stone.
intro.cn: calculate 来自拉丁语里表示计数石子的词。

items.en: calculus meant a small stone used for counting.
items.cn: 拉丁语 calculus 指用来计数的小石子。

items.en: calculare meant to reckon with such stones.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 calculare 意为用小石子核算。

items.en: calculen named working out an amount.
items.cn: 中古英语 calculen 指算出数量。

items.en: The word extended to judging and planning.
items.cn: 十七世纪词义扩展到判断与谋划。

items.en: Calculate covers arithmetic, estimation and intention.
items.cn: 现代英语中 calculate 兼指运算、估计与用意。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the calcul- base; the near-meaning group gives other number verbs.
note.cn: 形近组共用 calcul- 词基；近义组是其他与数字有关的动词。

entries.definition: the process or result of calculating
entries.definitionCN: 计算过程或结果

entries.definition: a device for doing arithmetic
entries.definitionCN: 计算器

entries.definition: done on purpose
entries.definitionCN: 蓄意的

entries.definition: to work out an amount with numbers
entries.definitionCN: 用数字算出结果

entries.definition: to judge an amount roughly
entries.definitionCN: 大致估算

entries.definition: to say numbers in order or find a total
entries.definitionCN: 数数或求总数

normalIntro.en: Calculate is built on the Latin word for a counting stone.
normalIntro.cn: calculate 建立在拉丁语「计数石子」这个词上。

normal.en: The noun is calculation.
normal.cn: 名词是 calculation。

normal.en: The device is a calculator.
normal.cn: 计算工具是 calculator。

normal.en: Calculated can mean deliberate.
normal.cn: calculated 可表示蓄意的。

normal.en: Calculating can mean shrewd.
normal.cn: calculating 可表示精明的。

normal.en: Calculate the cost is a common phrase.
normal.cn: calculate the cost 是常见搭配。

abstract.en: See pebbles lined up in rows on a table.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上石子排成一行行。

abstract.en: See a pencil adding figures down a page.
abstract.cn: 想象铅笔在纸上把数字一列列相加。

abstract.en: See a plan drawn before the words are spoken.
abstract.cn: 想象话未出口，打算已经画好。

examples.en: He calculated the total cost carefully.
examples.cn: 他仔细计算了总花费。

examples.en: We calculated that the trip would take three hours.
examples.cn: 我们估计这趟行程要三个小时。

examples.en: The remark was calculated to calm the crowd.
examples.cn: 那句话意在安抚人群。

dict_mnemonic.text: calculate 里有 calc，像 chalk 粉笔，粉笔在纸上列数字、一行行算，算出结果就是 calculate。

root: calculate 源自拉丁语 calculus（计数用的小石子），动词 calculare 意为用小石子核算，后来泛指一切数值运算，并引申出估计与谋划。

sensesIntro.en: Working out numbers, judging roughly, and planning an effect.
sensesIntro.cn: 数值运算、大致判断，以及预先谋划效果。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: counting stones moved into rows.
core.cn: 核心意象：计数石子被排成一行行。

branches.en: calculate the cost
branches.cn: 计算成本

branches.en: calculate the distance
branches.cn: 计算距离

branches.en: calculate that it will rain
branches.cn: 估计会下雨

branches.en: calculated to calm the crowd
branches.cn: 意在安抚人群

branches.en: calculate accurately
branches.cn: 准确计算

intro.en: Calculate takes -ion, -or and -ed to make new words.
intro.cn: calculate 能加 -ion、-or 与 -ed 构成新词。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin calculus, a counting stone.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是拉丁语 calculus，意为计数石子。

a counting stone, later a branch of maths

definition_zh: 啪地折断；猛咬；快照；厉声说
definition_en: to break with a sharp sound, to bite suddenly, to take a quick photo, or to speak sharply
core_image: 一根树枝在重压下啪地断成两截
scene: 树枝在重压下啪地断了。 The branch snapped under the weight.
sceneCN: 这里 snap 是「啪地折断」（第 1 个义项）；句意：树枝在重压下啪地断了。

senses.title: Break with a sharp sound
senses.definition: to break suddenly with a short sharp sound
senses.definitionCN: 伴随短促尖利的声音突然断裂
senses.example: The branch snapped under the weight.
senses.exampleCN: 树枝在重压下啪地断了。
senses.why: This is the central physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心的物理义项。

senses.title: Bite suddenly
senses.definition: to bite something suddenly and quickly
senses.definitionCN: 突然迅速地咬住某物
senses.example: The dog snapped at the fly.
senses.exampleCN: 狗猛地去咬那只苍蝇。
senses.why: A quick bite has the same suddenness.
senses.whyCN: 快速咬合也有同样的突然性。

senses.title: Quick photograph
senses.definition: a quick photograph taken without much preparation
senses.definitionCN: 没有太多准备就快速拍下的照片
senses.example: She snapped a photo of the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 她给那座桥拍了张快照。
senses.why: The shutter makes a small snap.
senses.whyCN: 快门会发出轻轻的咔嚓声。

senses.title: Speak sharply
senses.definition: to speak to someone in a sudden angry way
senses.definitionCN: 突然生气地对某人说话
senses.example: He snapped at me for being late.
senses.exampleCN: 他因为我迟到而厉声斥责我。
senses.why: An angry reply snaps like a dry branch.
senses.whyCN: 愤怒的回应像枯枝一样啪地断裂。

intro.en: Snap came into English from Middle Low German.
intro.cn: snap 从中古低地德语进入英语。

items.en: Snappen meant to bite quickly.
items.cn: snappen 意为迅速咬住。

items.en: The word entered English as snap.
items.cn: 这个词以 snap 进入英语。

items.en: It named a sudden break.
items.cn: 它指突然的断裂。

items.en: It named a quick photograph.
items.cn: 它指快速拍下的照片。

items.en: Snap at someone means answer sharply.
items.cn: snap at 某人意为厉声回答。

note.en: Snap is compared with look-alike words and words for sudden actions.
note.cn: 把 snap 与形近词以及表示突然动作的词作比较。

entries.definition: to cut with small quick strokes
entries.definitionCN: 剪

entries.definition: a short sleep
entries.definitionCN: 小睡

entries.definition: to hit with an open hand
entries.definitionCN: 拍打

entries.definition: to cut with the teeth
entries.definitionCN: 咬

entries.definition: to come apart
entries.definitionCN: 断裂

entries.definition: to make a sharp sound or split
entries.definitionCN: 裂开；发爆裂声

normalIntro.en: Snap is a sudden action with a sharp sound.
normalIntro.cn: snap 是伴随尖利声响的突然动作。

normal.en: The branch snapped under the weight.
normal.cn: 树枝在重压下啪地断了。

normal.en: The dog snapped at the fly.
normal.cn: 狗猛地去咬那只苍蝇。

normal.en: She snapped a photo of the bridge.
normal.cn: 她给那座桥拍了张快照。

normal.en: He snapped at me for being late.
normal.cn: 他因为我迟到而厉声斥责我。

normal.en: The cold snap froze the pond.
normal.cn: 寒潮把池塘冻住了。

abstract.en: A temper can snap faster than a dry stick.
abstract.cn: 脾气可能比枯枝断得更快。

abstract.en: Some moments are worth a snap, not a speech.
abstract.cn: 有些瞬间值得拍张照，而不是发表演讲。

abstract.en: The smallest sound can announce the largest break.
abstract.cn: 最小的声响可能宣告最大的断裂。

examples.en: The branch snapped under the weight.
examples.cn: 树枝在重压下啪地断了。

examples.en: The dog snapped at the fly.
examples.cn: 狗猛地去咬那只苍蝇。

examples.en: She snapped a photo of the bridge.
examples.cn: 她给那座桥拍了张快照。

dict_mnemonic.text: snap 与 snip、nap、slap 形近；snap a photo 是「拍快照」，cold snap 是「寒潮」。

root: 经中古低地德语 snappen（迅速咬住）进入英语，核心义「突然而短促的动作」。

sensesIntro.en: Snap means to break sharply, bite, photograph quickly, or speak angrily.
sensesIntro.cn: snap 指啪地折断、猛咬、快速拍照，或生气地说话。

core.en: A sudden event with a sharp edge.
core.cn: 带有尖利感的突然事件。

branches.en: A branch gives way.
branches.cn: 树枝承受不住而断裂。

branches.en: Jaws close in a moment.
branches.cn: 上下颚瞬间合拢。

branches.en: A shutter records a second.
branches.cn: 快门记录下一秒。

branches.en: An angry voice cuts the air.
branches.cn: 愤怒的声音划破空气。

branches.en: Breaking and scolding share a sharp sound.
branches.cn: 折断与斥责共享一种尖利声响。

intro.en: Snap builds words for sudden breaks and quick shots.
intro.cn: snap 构成表示突然断裂和快速拍摄的词。

latinIntro.en: Snap is Germanic in origin, not Latin.
latinIntro.cn: snap 源自日耳曼语，不是拉丁语。

items.example: The rope will snap if you pull.
The string snapped in the wind.
The fire was snapping and crackling.
He took a snapshot of the square.
The case has a snap-on lid.

items.meaning: a short period of very cold weather
items.example: A cold snap killed the young plants.

definition_zh: 未知的；不著名的；陌生的；未知的事物；无名者
definition_en: not known, not identified, or not famous, or a person or thing that is not known
core_image: 一张地图的边缘渐渐变淡，最后化成一片没有标注的空白，只写着「未探明」
scene: 侦探把照片翻过来，背面没有一个字，只有一枚模糊的指纹。 The identity of the caller remains unknown.
sceneCN: 这里 unknown 是「未知的、不为人知的」（第 1 个义项：尚不被知道）；句意为来电者的身份仍然不明。地图上那片没被标注的空白，就是这个词的样子。

derivatives.zh: 由古英语 uncuð 一类形式经 know 加 -able 构成，义为「不可知的」
由 unknown 的词干加 -ingly 构成，义为「不知不觉地」
本词的复数，义为「若干未知因素」
本词去掉 un-，义为「已知的；著名的」

senses.title: Not known at all
senses.definition: not known to anyone, or not yet discovered or understood
senses.definitionCN: 尚不为人所知，或尚未被发现与理解
senses.example: The cause of the fire is still unknown.
senses.exampleCN: 起火的原因仍不清楚。
senses.why: Un- denies and know supplies the knowing: the fact has not been reached by any mind.
senses.whyCN: un- 表示否定，know 提供「知道」：这个事实还没有被任何头脑触及。

senses.title: Not identified
senses.definition: not recognized or identified, as of a person, a name, or a source
senses.definitionCN: 不能辨认或确认，如某个人、某个名字或某个来源
senses.example: Police are searching for an unknown man seen near the bank.
senses.exampleCN: 警方正在寻找一名在银行附近被看到的身份不明男子。
senses.why: Here the thing exists but its label is missing; the gap is in identification.
senses.whyCN: 这里事物存在，缺的是标签；空缺在身份辨认上。

senses.title: Not famous
senses.definition: not well known to the public, though perhaps respected by a few
senses.definitionCN: 不为公众所知，虽然可能被少数人看重
senses.example: The painting was bought for a small sum from an unknown artist.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅画以很低的价钱从一位不出名的画家那里买来。
senses.why: Reputation is a kind of knowing held by many; if few know you, you are unknown.
senses.whyCN: 名声是许多人所持有的一种知道；知道你的少，你就是不为人知。

senses.title: The unknown as a whole
senses.definition: with the, the part of the world or of knowledge not yet explored or understood
senses.definitionCN: 与 the 连用，指世界或知识中尚未被探索与理解的部分
senses.example: Explorers in those years were drawn to the unknown.
senses.exampleCN: 那些年的探险者被未知吸引。
senses.why: An adjective of state becomes a noun for the whole region no one has entered.
senses.whyCN: 表示状态的形容词转成了名词，指没人进入过的那一整片区域。

senses.title: A person without a name
senses.definition: with a, someone whose name is not known, as in an unknown soldier
senses.definitionCN: 与 a 连用，指名字不为所知的人，如无名战士
senses.example: A stone in the square honours the unknown who fell in the war.
senses.exampleCN: 广场上的一块石头纪念战争中阵亡的无名者。
senses.why: The word names the person by what is missing, which is why it can honour them.
senses.whyCN: 这个词以「缺少的东西」来命名人，因此它能够用来致敬。

intro.en: Unknown began as a native Old English compound and has kept the same shape for a thousand years.
intro.cn: unknown 起初是古英语本土复合词，一千年来形式几乎未变。

items.en: Un- denied and cnāwan meant to know; the compound uncūþ covered what was not known.
items.cn: un- 是否定前缀，cnāwan 意为「知道」；复合词 uncūþ 指所不知道的事物。

items.en: Norse influence helped know and its forms settle as the everyday words of England.
items.cn: 诺尔斯语影响使 know 及其种种形式成为英格兰日常用语。

items.en: The form settled as unknow(e)n, spelled closer to the modern word.
items.cn: 中古英语中形式固定为 unknow(e)n，拼写接近现代。

items.en: The word spread from facts to people, becoming a title for the anonymous, as in the unknown soldier.
items.cn: 这个词从事实扩展到人，成为无名者的称谓，如无名战士。

items.en: Science and mathematics made the noun common, as in unknowns in an equation.
items.cn: 科学与数学使名词用法普及，如方程中的未知数。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers other words in un- and forms of know; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives for what is not familiar or not certain.
note.cn: 形近组收其他以 un- 构成的词以及 know 的各种形式；近义组收表示不熟悉或不确定的形容词。

entries.definition: The adjective for what is recognized or widely known.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「已知的、著名的」，与本词相反。

entries.definition: Beyond any possibility of being known.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不可知的」，根本无从得知。

entries.definition: Without being aware of it; the word describes a person's action.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「不知不觉地」，描述人的行为。

entries.definition: Not known because not met before; it stresses lack of acquaintance.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不熟悉的」，强调没有接触过。

entries.definition: Going without being seen or heeded.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「未被注意到的」。

entries.definition: Not easy to understand; the facts exist but are dim.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不清楚的」，事实存在但模糊。

entries.definition: Of a person whose name is not given; formal and common in writing.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「匿名的」，较正式，多用于书面。

entries.definition: Little known, or hard to see; often used of writers and words.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「鲜为人知的、晦涩的」，多用于作者与词语。

entries.definition: Not settled or sure; it describes doubt rather than absence of knowledge.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不确定的」，描述怀疑而非知识的缺失。

entries.definition: Strange and hard to explain, often with a feeling of secrecy.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「神秘的」，带有秘密的气氛。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the plain un- plus know structure and the phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用 un 加 know 的朴素结构，以及这个词常用的搭配。

normal.en: Un- means not and know is to know: literally not known.
normal.cn: un- 表示「不」，know 是「知道」：字面就是不被知道。

normal.en: Unknown to me means I was never told.
normal.cn: unknown to me 意为从来没人告诉过我。

normal.en: The unknown soldier is honoured precisely because his name is missing.
normal.cn: 无名战士之所以受纪念，恰恰因为名字缺失。

normal.en: In an equation the unknowns are the letters you must solve for.
normal.cn: 方程中的未知数就是你要解出的那些字母。

normal.en: The opposite is simply known.
normal.cn: 其反面就是 known。

abstract.en: Picture the edge of an old map fading into blank paper: what is missing is not nothing, but unwritten space.
abstract.cn: 想象旧地图的边缘淡成空白纸：缺的不是「没有」，而是尚未写下的空间。

abstract.en: Unknown is a word about the limits of a mind, not about the thing itself.
abstract.cn: unknown 说的是头脑的界限，而不是事物本身。

abstract.en: Every discovery begins as an unknown that nobody had yet named.
abstract.cn: 每一项发现最初都是一个还没人命名过的未知。

examples.en: The exact number of birds on the island is unknown.
examples.cn: 岛上鸟的确切数量未知。

examples.en: An unknown woman returned the lost wallet to the desk.
examples.cn: 一位不知名的女子把丢失的钱包交到了前台。

examples.en: They set out into the unknown with three weeks of food.
examples.cn: 他们带着三周的食物走向未知。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安的弄恩」——安对此弄不明白，全然不知：未知的

root: 由否定前缀 un- 与古英语动词 cnāwan「知道」（今 know）构成，古英语作 uncūþ，中古英语写作 unknow(e)n；由「不被知道」扩展到身份不明、不出名，并名词化为未知之物与无名者。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of unknown all mark a gap in knowing: a fact not reached, a face not identified, a name not famous, a region unexplored, or a person without a name.
sensesIntro.cn: unknown 的五个义项都标记认知上的空缺：未被触及的事实、未被辨认的面孔、不出名的名字、未被探索的区域，或没有名字的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the edge of a map fading into blank paper with nothing written there.
core.cn: 核心意象：地图边缘淡成白纸，上面什么都没有写。

branches.en: THE FACT: something true that nobody has found out yet.
branches.cn: 事实线：确实存在却还没人查明的事情。

branches.en: THE FACE: the person is present, the identity is missing.
branches.cn: 面孔线：人在那里，身份却是空白。

branches.en: THE NAME: few people know him, though he may deserve it.
branches.cn: 名字线：知道他的人很少，尽管他可能值得被知道。

branches.en: THE REGION: the noun names the whole unexplored part.
branches.cn: 区域线：名词化后指整片未被探索之处。

branches.en: THE UNNAMED: honouring those whose names were never recorded.
branches.cn: 无名线：用来致敬那些名字从未被记下的人。

intro.en: Unknown is entirely native: a Germanic negative prefix on an Old English verb, with no Latin element at all.
intro.cn: unknown 完全是本土构造：日耳曼语否定前缀加古英语动词，不含任何拉丁成分。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin in this word; the table lists later Latin-based synonyms that cover the same gap.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词里没有拉丁成分；下表列出后世以拉丁语为源、指同样空缺的近义词。

items.example: The verb supplies the act that is missing.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供缺失的那个动作。

items.example: The older native form of know.
The oldest recorded form of the word.
items.exampleCN: 这个词最古老的记录形式。
一个正式的拉丁语来源近义词。

definition_zh: 例行公事；惯例；固定流程；日常的
definition_en: a usual order of actions, a set performance, or ordinary and regular
core_image: 每天清晨重复的固定流程
scene: 她早晨的例行公事从一杯茶开始。 Her morning routine begins with a cup of tea.
sceneCN: 这里 routine 是「例行公事」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她早晨的例行公事从一杯茶开始。

senses.title: Daily habit
senses.definition: the usual order in which you do things every day
senses.definitionCN: 每天做事的固定顺序与习惯
senses.example: Exercise is part of his daily routine.
senses.exampleCN: 锻炼是他日常安排的一部分。
senses.why: The same steps repeat at the same time.
senses.whyCN: 同样的步骤在同样时间重复。

senses.title: Set sequence
senses.definition: a fixed set of movements or actions in a performance
senses.definitionCN: 表演中一套固定的动作或流程
senses.example: The skaters practiced their routine for hours.
senses.exampleCN: 滑冰者练习他们的套路练了好几个小时。
senses.why: A rehearsed order is followed without breaks.
senses.whyCN: 排练好的顺序被不间断地执行。

senses.title: Ordinary
senses.definition: ordinary and done as a regular part of work
senses.definitionCN: 普通的、作为工作常规部分进行的
senses.example: The staff handle routine questions quickly.
senses.exampleCN: 员工们迅速处理日常问题。
senses.why: What repeats becomes ordinary and expected.
senses.whyCN: 重复之事变得普通而可预期。

intro.en: Routine is French route plus -ine, a usual course.
intro.cn: routine 是法语 route 加 -ine，意为惯常的路程。

items.en: Route means a way or course.
items.cn: route 意为道路或行程。

items.en: The suffix -ine marks a manner or practice.
items.cn: 后缀 -ine 标记方式或做法。

items.en: Routine names the usual way of acting.
items.cn: routine 指惯常的行为方式。

items.en: English routine keeps the daily order sense.

normalIntro.en: A routine is the usual road you walk each day.
normalIntro.cn: routine 是你每天走的惯常之路。

normal.en: A walk after dinner is part of my routine.
normal.cn: 晚饭后散步是我日常安排的一部分。

normal.en: The team follows a strict morning routine.
normal.cn: 团队遵循严格的晨间流程。

normal.en: The pair practiced a new dance routine.
normal.cn: 这对搭档练习了一套新舞蹈动作。

normal.en: Routine work fills most of the morning.
normal.cn: 日常工作占去大半个上午。

normal.en: A short trip can break the routine.
normal.cn: 一次短途旅行可以打破常规。

abstract.en: Picture the same steps taken at the same hour.
abstract.cn: 想象同一时刻重复同样的步骤。

abstract.en: Imagine a well-worn path across a lawn.
abstract.cn: 想象草坪上被踏出的一条小路。

abstract.en: Think of a clock marking an identical day.
abstract.cn: 想象时钟标记着一模一样的一天。

examples.en: The nurse checks each patient on her routine.
examples.cn: 护士按例行流程检查每位病人。

examples.en: He changed his routine after the move.
examples.cn: 搬家后他改变了日常习惯。

examples.en: The show ended with a comic routine.
examples.cn: 演出以一段滑稽表演收尾。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「route（路）＋ ine」——每天走同一条路，做同一套事，就是例行公事与固定流程。

root: 法语 route（道路）＋ -ine → routine，核心义「惯常走的那条路」。

sensesIntro.en: Routine means a daily habit, a fixed performance sequence, or ordinary regular work.
sensesIntro.cn: routine 意为日常习惯、固定的表演流程，或常规普通的工作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the same steps at the same hour.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一时刻重复的同样步骤。

branches.en: The daily habit is the main sense.
branches.cn: 日常习惯是主要义项。

branches.en: A performance follows a fixed sequence.
branches.cn: 表演遵循固定顺序。

branches.en: What repeats becomes ordinary work.
branches.cn: 重复之事成为常规工作。

branches.en: Both are orders followed without thought.
branches.cn: 两者都是无须多想就遵循的顺序。

branches.en: Habit and ordinary work share repetition.
branches.cn: 习惯与常规工作共享重复性。

intro.en: Routine builds on French route, a course or way.
intro.cn: routine 建立在法语 route（路程、道路）之上。

latinIntro.en: Route goes back to Latin rupta via, a cleared road.
latinIntro.cn: route 可追溯到拉丁语 rupta via，意为开辟的道路。

items.example: Route is the base of routine.
items.exampleCN: route 是 routine 的基础。

items.example: Routine keeps the worn path image.
items.exampleCN: routine 保留踏熟路径的意象。

latinEntries.example: Rupta lies behind route and routine.
latinEntries.exampleCN: rupta 是 route 与 routine 的深层来源。

definition_zh: 由…组成；在于；与…一致
definition_en: to be made up of particular parts, or to have something as its central point
core_image: 一只碗里盛着几样分辨得清的配料
scene: 厨师示范前先说明汤里放了什么。 The soup consists of tomatoes, beans and a little salt.
sceneCN: 这里 consist 指「由…组成」（第 1 个义项：整体由若干部分构成）；句意是这道汤由番茄、豆子和少量盐组成。

senses.title: Made of parts
senses.definition: to be made up of particular parts or elements
senses.definitionCN: 整体由若干具体部分构成
senses.example: The team consists of six engineers.
senses.exampleCN: 这个团队由六名工程师组成。
senses.why: You cannot name a whole without naming what stands inside it.
senses.whyCN: 要说清一个整体，就得说清里面站着什么。

senses.title: Lying in
senses.definition: to have something as its essential point or quality
senses.definitionCN: 以某事为其根本要点或性质
senses.example: True comfort consists in wanting less.
senses.exampleCN: 真正的自在在于欲求更少。
senses.why: Some things are not built of parts but rest on one idea.
senses.whyCN: 有些事物不是由零件搭成，而是靠一个念头立住。

senses.title: Standing together
senses.definition: to be in agreement with something, an older and rarer sense
senses.definitionCN: 与某事物相符合，是较古老且少用的义项
senses.example: The two reports consist with each other.
senses.exampleCN: 这两份报告彼此吻合。
senses.why: Things that stand together also tend to tell the same story.
senses.whyCN: 站在一起的东西，往往也讲着同一个故事。

intro.en: Consist comes from Latin consistere, to stand together, built from com-, together, and sistere, to stand.
intro.cn: consist 来自拉丁语 consistere，意为站在一起，由 com-（一起）与 sistere（站立）构成。

items.en: Sistere meant to stand still or take a stand.
items.cn: sistere 意为站定或站住立场。

items.en: Consistere meant to take a firm position together.
items.cn: consistere 意为一起站定位置。

items.en: Later Latin gave it the sense of being made of parts.
items.cn: 后来的拉丁语赋予它由部分构成的含义。

items.en: French consister narrowed to being composed of something.
items.cn: 法语 consister 收窄为由某物构成。

items.en: English consist kept both the standing and the composed senses.
items.cn: 英语 consist 同时保留了站定与构成两层意思。

items.en: Today the pattern consist of is by far the most common.
items.cn: 今天 consist of 这一搭配最为常用。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin stand base sist-, and the meaning group names other ways of saying what a whole is made of.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语的站立词基 sist-，近义组列出其他表示整体由何构成的说法。

entries.definition: always behaving or happening in the same way
entries.definitionCN: 一贯的；前后一致的

entries.definition: to say firmly that something must happen
entries.definitionCN: 坚持；坚决要求

entries.definition: to keep going even when it is hard
entries.definitionCN: 坚持；持续

entries.definition: to have particular parts as its contents
entries.definitionCN: 包含；由…构成

entries.definition: to make up the parts of a whole
entries.definitionCN: 组成；构成

entries.definition: to have something inside
entries.definitionCN: 容纳；包含

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from parts standing together, then move to the one point a thing rests on and to old agreement.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从各部分站在一起开始，再到一件事所依托的那个要点，最后到古老的相一致义。

normal.en: Con- is together and sist is stand, so consist is parts standing together.
normal.cn: con- 是一起，sist 是站立，consist 就是各部分站在一起。

normal.en: Take the soup apart in your mind, and you have consist of.
normal.cn: 在心里把那碗汤拆开来看，你就得到了 consist of。

normal.en: Consist of names the parts, while consist in names the point.
normal.cn: consist of 点出部分，consist in 点出要害。

normal.en: A chair consists of legs, a seat and a back, yet you still see one chair.
normal.cn: 椅子由腿、座面和靠背组成，可你看到的仍是一把椅子。

normal.en: Ask what it is made of, then ask what it really rests on.
normal.cn: 先问它由什么做成，再问它究竟靠什么立住。

abstract.en: Picture four stones holding up one flat slab.
abstract.cn: 想象四块石头托起一块平板。

abstract.en: Picture a row of ingredients laid beside a pot.
abstract.cn: 想象一排配料摆在锅边。

abstract.en: Picture a rope made of many thin threads.
abstract.cn: 想象一根由许多细线拧成的绳子。

examples.en: The course consists of ten short lessons.
examples.cn: 这门课由十节短课组成。

examples.en: Happiness does not consist in having more.
examples.cn: 幸福并不在于拥有更多。

examples.en: A good meal consists of simple things done well.
examples.cn: 一顿好饭由几样做得到位的简单食材组成。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 consist 记成 con（一起）加 sist（站立）：几样东西站在一起构成一个整体，就是由…组成。

root: 源自拉丁语 consistere（com 一起 + sistere 站立），本义是一起站定，后指由若干部分构成、要点在于。

sensesIntro.en: From parts standing together, to the point a thing rests on, and at last to an older sense of agreement.
sensesIntro.cn: 从各部分站在一起，到一件事所依托的要点，最后到较为古老的相一致之义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: several stones standing shoulder to shoulder under one slab.
core.cn: 核心意象：几块石头并肩立在同一块石板之下。

branches.en: The commonest sense simply lists what a whole is made of.
branches.cn: 最常用的义项只是列出整体由什么构成。

branches.en: The second sense points to the one idea a thing rests on.
branches.cn: 第二个义项指向一件事所依托的那一个念头。

branches.en: The old sense says two things can stand without contradiction.
branches.cn: 古老义项说的是两件事能并立而不相矛盾。

branches.en: Both senses answer the question of what something really is.
branches.cn: 两个义项都在回答某物究竟是什么。

branches.en: A thing that rests on one point can also agree with another.
branches.cn: 依托于一个要点的事物，也能与另一事物相合。

intro.en: Consist is built on Latin com-, together, plus sistere, to stand.
intro.cn: consist 由拉丁语 com-（一起）与 sistere（站立）构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin stand base sist- also appears in insist, persist and resist.

definition_en: based on facts rather than personal feelings, or a goal that one aims to reach
