senses.title: The Object in the Mind: the 1610s philosophical sense
senses.titleCN: 心中的对象：17 世纪初的哲学义
senses.definition: in 1610s philosophy, existing as perceived or thought, ideal, representative, or phenomenal, as opposed to subjective or formal
senses.definitionCN: 17 世纪初哲学中，指作为被感知或被思考之物而存在的、观念的、表象的、现象的，与 subjective 或 formal 相对
senses.example: In the old debate, pain was called objective when considered as a thought rather than a bodily state.
senses.exampleCN: 在那场古老争论中，痛苦被当作思想而非身体状态来看时，被称为 objective。
senses.why: The word was built from objectum, 'a thing put before the mind'. In the 1610s that thing was still inside the mind, so objective meant 'existing as an object of thought'.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 objectum“被摆到心智面前的东西”构成。17 世纪初，这东西还在心智之内，所以 objective 意为“作为思想对象而存在”。

senses.title: The Real Thing Outside: independent of the mind
senses.titleCN: 心外实物：不依赖心智而存在
senses.definition: real and existing independently of the mind, belonging to the object of knowledge rather than to the observer
senses.definitionCN: 真实存在、不依赖心智的，属于认知对象而非观察者的
senses.example: The mountain has an objective existence whether or not anyone looks at it.
senses.exampleCN: 无论是否有人看它，这座山都客观存在。
senses.why: From the mid-17th century the 'object' was pushed outside: what is objective is what belongs to the thing known, not to the knower. The sense almost reverses the older one.
senses.whyCN: 从 17 世纪中期起，“对象”被推到心智之外：objective 的东西属于被认识的事物，而不属于认识者。这个义项几乎翻转了旧义。

senses.title: Without a Personal Lens: impartial
senses.titleCN: 不戴个人镜片：不偏不倚
senses.definition: not influenced by personal feelings, interests, or bias when judging
senses.definitionCN: 判断时不受个人情感、利益或偏见影响
senses.example: A judge must remain objective even when the case is emotionally charged.
senses.exampleCN: 即使案件牵动情绪，法官也必须保持客观。
senses.why: If truth belongs to the object, the observer should stop adding private colour. The 18th-century sense, strengthened through German translations, names that disciplined detachment.
senses.whyCN: 如果真相属于对象，观察者就该停止添加私人色彩。18 世纪经德语译介强化的义项，命名的正是这种克制的抽离。

senses.title: What the Evidence Shows: fact-based
senses.titleCN: 证据所示：以事实为依据
senses.definition: based on observable facts and evidence that others can check
senses.definitionCN: 建立在他人可以核查的可观察事实与证据之上
senses.example: The report gives an objective account of the accident, with times and measurements.
senses.exampleCN: 报告用时间和测量数据，对事故作了客观陈述。
senses.why: An account is objective when it stays with what was put before the senses: times, measurements, records. Evidence replaces opinion as the measure.
senses.whyCN: 当陈述停留在摆在感官之前的东西——时间、测量、记录——它就是客观的。证据取代意见成为量尺。

senses.title: The Point to Be Taken: a military objective
senses.definition: a place or position that an army aims to capture or hold, from which the general noun use grew
senses.definitionCN: 军队意图夺取或守住的地点或阵地，名词的一般用法由此而来
senses.example: The hill was the objective of the night attack.
senses.exampleCN: 那座山头是夜袭的目标。
senses.why: Military language used objective for the point set before the force, the thing to be taken. The target on the map is literally 'the object put in front'.
senses.whyCN: 军事语言用 objective 指摆在部队前方的点，即要夺取的东西。地图上的目标字面上就是“被摆在前面的对象”。

senses.title: The Aim: a goal to reach
senses.definition: a goal or aim that a person or organization works toward
senses.definitionCN: 个人或组织努力要达到的目标
senses.example: Our main objective is to cut waiting times by half.
senses.exampleCN: 我们的主要目标是把等待时间减少一半。
senses.why: Once the military target became general, any planned end point could be an objective: something placed ahead of you that guides effort.
senses.whyCN: 军事目标一旦泛化，任何计划中的终点都可以叫 objective：一个摆在你前方、引导努力的东西。

senses.title: The Lens Facing the Object
senses.definition: in optics, the lens or lens system nearest the object being viewed, as in a microscope or telescope
senses.definitionCN: 光学中离被观察物体最近的那片透镜或透镜组，如显微镜或望远镜的物镜
senses.example: Clean the objective before examining the slide.
senses.exampleCN: 检查玻片前先清洁物镜。
senses.why: The optical objective is the lens turned toward the object, not toward the eye. The same 'thing before you' image is used in a physical instrument.
senses.whyCN: 光学物镜是朝向物体、而不是朝向眼睛的那片镜片。同一个“摆在面前的东西”的意象被用在一件实体仪器上。

senses.title: The Object Case: grammar
senses.definition: in grammar, the case of a noun or pronoun that is the object of a verb or preposition
senses.definitionCN: 语法中名词或代词作动词或介词宾语时的格
senses.example: In 'she saw him', him is in the objective case.
senses.exampleCN: 在 she saw him 中，him 是宾格。
senses.why: Grammar names the receiver of the action the object. The objective case is simply the form a word takes when it stands as the object before the verb.
senses.whyCN: 语法把动作的承受者称为 object。宾格就是当一个词作为动词的宾语出现时所取的形式。

senses.title: Description Without Interpretation
senses.titleCN: 不带解释的描述：客观呈现
senses.definition: presenting what can be seen or measured without adding interpretation, as in objective reporting or photography
senses.definitionCN: 只呈现可见或可测的内容而不添加解释，如客观报道或客观摄影
senses.example: The photographer took an objective record of the building before demolition.
senses.exampleCN: 摄影师在拆除前对建筑作了客观记录。
senses.why: The final extension keeps the observer out of the frame. What is recorded is the object as it stands, with no story laid over it.
senses.whyCN: 最后的延伸把观察者请出画面。被记录的是对象本来的样子，上面没有叠加任何故事。

intro.en: Objective is object plus -ive. Object came from Latin obiectum 'thing put before', and objective first meant 'existing as an object of thought' before its sense moved outside the mind to 'real' and then to 'impartial'.
intro.cn: objective 是 object 加 -ive。object 来自拉丁语 obiectum“被摆到面前的东西”，而 objective 最初指“作为思想对象而存在”，后来移出心智，变成“真实的”，再变成“不偏不倚的”。

items.en: First used as a philosophical term meaning 'as perceived or thought; ideal; representative; phenomenal', opposed to subjective or formal.
items.cn: 最初作哲学术语，意为“被感知或被思考的；观念的；表象的；现象的”，与 subjective 或 formal 相对。

items.en: The sense 'belonging to the real object of knowledge, real' appears, in contrast with subjective; the meaning almost reverses the earlier one.
items.cn: 出现“属于认知的实在对象、真实的”义，与 subjective 相对；含义几乎翻转了早先的义项。

items.en: The modern sense 'unbiased, not shaped by personal feeling' is strengthened through German philosophical translations.
items.cn: 现代义“客观的、不带偏见的”经德语哲学译介而强化。

items.en: Formed on medieval Latin objectivus, used by Duns Scotus, from objectum 'thing put before'.
items.cn: 按中世纪拉丁语 objectivus 构成，邓斯·司各脱曾使用，出自 objectum“被摆到面前的东西”。

items.en: Objectum is the neuter noun use of obiectus, past participle of obicere 'to throw before': ob 'in front of, towards, against' plus iacere 'to throw' (PIE *ye- 'to throw, impel').
items.cn: objectum 是 obiectus 的中性名词化；obiectus 为 obicere“投到前面”的过去分词：ob“在前、朝向、对着”+ iacere“投、掷”（原始印欧语 *ye-“投、推”）。

items.en: The noun 'objective' meaning a target comes from military usage, the point set before a force; the general sense 'goal' followed. Object itself dates from late 14c.
items.cn: 名词 objective 的“目标”义来自军事用语，即摆在部队前方的点；泛化的“目的”义随后出现。object 本身则始于 14 世纪晚期。

note.en: The look-alike group stays inside the object family and its -ive neighbours; the near-meaning group holds words that overlap with only part of objective.
note.cn: 形近组留在 object 词族及其 -ive 邻词内；近义组是只与 objective 部分义项重叠的词。

entries.definition: a thing that can be seen or touched, or something opposed. Objective is built from it, but the stress and the noun-verb split differ.
entries.definitionCN: 可见可触的物体，或反对的对象。objective 由它构成，但重音和名词／动词分工不同。

entries.definition: a statement of disagreement. It comes from object as a verb 'to oppose', not from objective.
entries.definitionCN: 反对的意见。它来自动词 object“反对”，而不是来自 objective。

entries.definition: a word that describes a noun. It shares the -ive ending and the Latin iacere 'throw' root, but its prefix is ad-, not ob-.
entries.definitionCN: 描述名词的词。它同样以 -ive 结尾，也含拉丁语 iacere“投”的词根，但前缀是 ad-，不是 ob-。

entries.definition: not favouring one side over another. It stresses fairness between parties, while objective stresses independence from one's own feelings.
entries.definitionCN: 不偏袒任何一方。它强调各方之间的公平，objective 强调独立于自己的情感。

entries.definition: free from prejudice or a settled leaning. It is close to objective but names the absence of bias rather than the presence of facts.
entries.definitionCN: 没有偏见或既定倾向。它接近 objective，但说的是“没有偏见”，而不是“依据事实”。

entries.definition: based on facts. It covers only the evidence sense of objective and says nothing about being a goal.
entries.definitionCN: 以事实为依据的。它只覆盖 objective 的证据义，与“目标”义无关。

normalIntro.en: Real links only: objectum is ob- 'before' plus iacere 'to throw', and objective is object plus -ive. The 1610s and modern senses are a recorded reversal, not an invented story.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实联系：objectum 是 ob-“在前”加 iacere“投”，objective 是 object 加 -ive。17 世纪初义与现代义是有记录的翻转，不是编造的故事。

normal.en: Objectum is ob- 'in front of' plus iacere 'to throw': a thing thrown before the mind or the eyes.
normal.cn: objectum 是 ob-“在前”加 iacere“投”：被投到心智或视线之前的东西。

normal.en: Objective is simply object plus -ive: 'relating to the object put before you'.
normal.cn: objective 就是 object 加 -ive：与“摆在你面前的对象”相关的。

normal.en: The 1610s sense meant 'in the mind'; the modern sense moved outside the mind to 'real'. The word reversed direction.
normal.cn: 17 世纪初的义项指“在心中的”；现代义移到心外，指“真实的”。这个词转了个方向。

normal.en: Objection and objective share object but pull opposite ways: one throws something against, the other looks at what is before.
normal.cn: objection 与 objective 都含 object，却朝相反方向拉：一个把东西扔过去反对，一个只看面前的东西。

normal.en: A military objective is the literal point set before a force; the everyday 'goal' grew from that target.
normal.cn: 军事 objective 是字面上摆在部队前方的点；日常的“目标”义从那个靶点长出来。

abstract.en: Picture an object alone under a lamp: the table, the wall and the observer all fall into shadow.
abstract.cn: 想象灯下只有一件东西：桌子、墙和观察者都落进阴影。

abstract.en: The observer steps back until their own shadow leaves the frame; that is the move from subjective to objective.
abstract.cn: 观察者后退，直到自己的影子离开画面；这就是从主观到客观的那一步。

abstract.en: Move the same object onto a map and it becomes a target: objective is now the point to be reached.
abstract.cn: 把同一件东西移到地图上，它就成了靶点：objective 此时是要到达的点。

examples.en: The study offers an objective measure of how noisy the streets are.
examples.cn: 这项研究提供了街道噪声程度的客观量度。

examples.en: Our objective for the year is to reduce waste by a third.
examples.cn: 我们今年的目标是把浪费减少三分之一。

examples.en: He tried to stay objective, but the photographs made him angry.
examples.cn: 他努力保持客观，但那些照片让他愤怒。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「啊不，接个物体」——先别急着评判，把摆在面前的物体接住看清楚 → objective 客观的、目标

root: 拉丁语 objectum“被摆到面前的东西”= ob“在前”+ iacere“投、掷”，加 -ive；objective 字面“与摆在面前的对象相关的”，由“客体”引出“客观”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of objective all turn on one act: throwing something in front. First it is an object of thought, then a real thing outside, then an impartial view, then a target on a map.
sensesIntro.cn: objective 的九个义项都围绕一个动作：把某物投到前方。它先是思想的对象，再是心外的实物，再是不偏不倚的看法，最后成为地图上的靶点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an object placed in front of the mind or the eyes.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件被摆到心智或视线之前的东西。

branches.en: THE OBJECT IN THE MIND: the 1610s philosophical sense, where the object is still a thought.
branches.cn: 心中的对象：17 世纪初的哲学义，对象仍是一种思想。

branches.en: REALITY AND EVIDENCE: the object outside the mind, and the facts that can be checked.
branches.cn: 现实与证据：心外的对象，以及可以核查的事实。

branches.en: THE DISCIPLINED OBSERVER: impartial judgment, and description without interpretation.
branches.cn: 受约束的观察者：不偏不倚的判断，以及不带解释的描述。

branches.en: THE AIM: a military point to be taken, and the general goal that grew from it.
branches.cn: 目标：要夺取的军事据点，以及由此长出的普通目的。

branches.en: TECHNICAL OBJECTS: the lens facing the object, and the grammatical object case.
branches.cn: 技术性对象：朝向物体的镜片，以及语法中的宾格。

intro.en: Objective is the Latin adjective objectivus in English form: object- plus -ive. The root sits in ob- 'before' and iacere 'to throw', the same root that gives subject, adjective and object.
intro.cn: objective 是拉丁形容词 objectivus 的英语形式：object- 加 -ive。词根在 ob-“在前”与 iacere“投”里，也是 subject、adjective、object 的共同来源。

latinIntro.en: Latin objectum 'thing put before' is the neuter noun from obicere; objectivus was used by Duns Scotus. The same iacere also builds subjectum 'thrown under' and adiectivus 'thrown to'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 objectum“被摆到前面之物”是 obicere 的中性名词；objectivus 由邓斯·司各脱使用。同一个 iacere 还构成 subjectum“投在下面”和 adiectivus“投向”。

items.meaning: relating to the object; impartial; a goal
items.meaningCN: 与对象相关的；客观的；目标（-ive 构成形容词，也可作名词）
items.example: The review aims to be objective.

items.meaningCN: 客观地；不带偏见地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The team judged the design objectively.
items.exampleCN: 团队客观地评估了这项设计。

items.meaningCN: 客观性；无偏见（-ity 构成状态名词）
items.example: Journalists are expected to maintain objectivity.

items.meaning: a thing put before the senses; to oppose
items.meaningCN: 物体；对象；反对（ob-“在前”+ iect“投”）
items.example: A strange object lay on the path.
items.exampleCN: 小路上躺着一个奇怪的物体。

items.meaning: a statement thrown against something; disagreement
items.meaningCN: 异议；反对（-ion 构成动作名词）

items.meaning: to treat as an object or make concrete
items.meaningCN: 使物化；使具体化（-ify 构成动词）
items.example: The advertisement objectifies the people it shows.
items.exampleCN: 这则广告把画面中的人物化了。

items.meaning: the act of treating someone as an object
items.meaningCN: 物化；对象化（-ication 构成名词）
items.example: The essay discusses the objectification of labour.
items.exampleCN: 这篇文章讨论劳动的物化。

items.meaning: literally 'thrown to'; a word added to a noun
items.meaningCN: 字面“投向”；形容词（加在名词上的词）
items.example: Choose a precise adjective for the noun.
items.exampleCN: 为这个名词选一个准确的形容词。

items.meaning: literally 'thrown under'; a topic or a grammatical subject
items.meaningCN: 字面“投在下面”；主题；主语
items.example: The subject of the talk was water.

items.meaning: based on personal feeling rather than the object

latinEntries.meaning: relating to an object; existing as an object of thought
latinEntries.meaningCN: 与对象相关的；作为思想对象存在的（邓斯·司各脱用语）

definition_zh: 激情；酷爱；强烈的情感；受难；盛怒
definition_en: a very strong feeling such as love or anger, a deep enthusiasm for something, the suffering of Christ in Christian teaching, or an old use for a fit of rage
core_image: 一个人伏在琴上，指尖用力，肩膀随旋律微微发抖
scene: 深夜的琴房里，一个人反复弹同一段旋律，额前的头发被汗粘住。 She played the sonata with a passion that surprised her teacher.
sceneCN: 这里的 passion 是「激情、强烈的情感」（第 1 个义项：强烈的情感）；句意是她以连老师都吃惊的激情演奏这首奏鸣曲。图中可辨识物件：琴键、乐谱、台灯。

pos.zh: 激情；酷爱；强烈的情感；受难；盛怒

collocations.zh: 情杀；因情感冲动犯下的罪

derivatives.zh: 由 passion 加形容词后缀 -ate 构成，义为「热情的；激烈的」
由 passionate 加 -ly 构成，义为「热烈地；激烈地」
由否定前缀 dis- 加 passionate 构成，义为「冷静的；不带感情的」
由 passion 加 -less（无）构成，义为「冷漠的；缺乏激情的」

senses.title: A very strong feeling
senses.definition: a very strong feeling, such as love, anger or grief, that takes hold of a person
senses.definitionCN: 抓住一个人的强烈情感，如爱、愤怒或悲痛
senses.example: She played the sonata with a passion that surprised her teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 她以连老师都吃惊的激情演奏这首奏鸣曲。
senses.why: Passion comes from a Latin word for suffering, so the noun first named what a person undergoes; strong feeling was seen as something that happens to you rather than something you choose.
senses.whyCN: passion 来自拉丁语中表示「受苦」的词，所以这个名词最初指人「承受」的东西；强烈情感被看成发生在你身上的事，而不是你挑选的事。

senses.title: A deep enthusiasm for something
senses.definition: an intense and lasting enthusiasm for an activity or subject, or the activity itself
senses.definitionCN: 对某项活动或主题持久而强烈的热情，也指这项活动本身
senses.example: His passion for old maps began in a dusty second-hand bookshop.
senses.exampleCN: 他对旧地图的酷爱始于一家满是灰尘的二手书店。
senses.why: If strong feeling can seize a person, it can also fasten on an object, and the thing so loved becomes the passion itself, which is why people speak of their passions as hobbies.
senses.whyCN: 既然强烈情感能抓住一个人，它也能牢牢附着在一个对象上，被如此热爱的东西本身就成了 passion，所以人们把自己热衷的爱好直接叫作 passions。

senses.title: The suffering of Christ
senses.definition: in Christian teaching, the suffering and death of Christ, especially as told in the Gospels
senses.definitionCN: 基督教教义中基督的受苦与死亡，尤指福音书所记
senses.example: The church holds a service to remember the Passion during Holy Week.
senses.exampleCN: 教会在圣周举行礼拜，纪念基督受难。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense of all: the Latin noun simply meant suffering, and the Gospel accounts of Christ's final days kept that plain meaning alive in English.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的一个义项：拉丁语名词本义就是「受苦」，福音书对基督最后几天的记述，让这个朴素的意思在英语里保存下来。

senses.title: A fit of rage
senses.definition: a sudden outburst of anger, used in older English especially in the phrase fly into a passion
senses.definitionCN: 突然爆发的愤怒，用于较早的英语，尤见于 fly into a passion 一语
senses.example: He flew into a passion when the clerk questioned his account.
senses.exampleCN: 店员质疑他的账目时，他勃然大怒。
senses.why: Because passion meant any strong feeling that takes you over, anger was one of its faces, and an outburst of anger was described as being seized by a passion.
senses.whyCN: 因为 passion 指任何一种占据你的强烈情感，愤怒也是它的一个面孔，所以一次暴怒就被说成被一股 passion 攫住。

intro.en: Passion descends from the Latin verb pati, to suffer, through the late Latin noun passio and Old French passion; the emotional senses grew out of the idea of being acted upon.
intro.cn: passion 由拉丁语动词 pati（受苦）经晚期拉丁语名词 passio 与古法语 passion 传下；那些情感义都是从「被作用于身」这一想法长出来的。

items.en: Pati meant to suffer, to endure or to undergo, and it is the root shared with patience and passive.
items.cn: pati 意为受苦、忍受、承受，是与 patience、passive 共有的词根。

items.en: Late Latin passio named suffering or a condition one undergoes; Christian writers used it for the suffering of Christ.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 passio 指受苦或人所承受的处境；基督教作者用它指基督的受难。

items.en: Old French passion carried both the religious sense and the wider sense of a strong emotion.
items.cn: 古法语 passion 同时带有宗教义与更宽泛的强烈情感义。

items.en: Middle English passion kept the religious sense first, then widened to love, grief and anger.
items.cn: 中古英语的 passion 最初保留宗教义，后来扩展到爱、悲痛与愤怒。

items.en: Modern English adds the everyday sense of an eager hobby, and keeps older idioms such as fly into a passion.
items.cn: 现代英语加上「热衷的爱好」这一日常义，并保留 fly into a passion 这类较早的说法。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words that share the Latin root for suffering or merely look alike; the near-meaning group collects words for intense feeling.
note.cn: 形近组收共享拉丁语「受苦」词根或只是长得像的词；近义组收表示强烈情感的词。

entries.definition: Receiving an action rather than doing it; built on the same Latin verb pati.
entries.definitionCN: 承受动作而非发出动作；同出拉丁语 pati。

entries.definition: The ability to wait or endure without complaint.
entries.definitionCN: 能够等待或忍受而不抱怨的能力。

entries.definition: Sympathy for the suffering of others, literally suffering with them.
entries.definitionCN: 对他人苦难的同情，字面义是「与之一同受苦」。

entries.definition: A way through or a section of a text; only the spelling is close, the origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 通道或文本的一段；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Intense enjoyment or interest in something.
entries.definitionCN: 对某事的强烈喜爱或兴趣。

entries.definition: Great energy or determination for a cause.
entries.definitionCN: 为某项事业投入的巨大热情或决心。

entries.definition: Very strong and sincere feeling, especially of belief.
entries.definitionCN: 极其强烈而真挚的感情，尤指信念。

entries.definition: Intense feeling of love or devotion, often literary.
entries.definitionCN: 强烈的爱意或献身之情，多用于文学。

normalIntro.en: Passion is built on a Latin verb for suffering, so every sense keeps the idea that a strong feeling is something a person undergoes rather than chooses.
normalIntro.cn: passion 建立在拉丁语表示「受苦」的动词之上，所以每个义项都保留一个想法：强烈情感是人承受的，而不是挑选的。

normal.en: Passion, patience, passive and compassion all come from Latin pati, to suffer, so the family is about what is done to you.
normal.cn: passion、patience、passive 与 compassion 都来自拉丁语 pati（受苦），所以这一族词说的都是「落到你身上的事」。

normal.en: The religious sense is the oldest: the Passion is what Christ underwent, not what he enjoyed.
normal.cn: 宗教义最古老：the Passion 是基督所承受的，而不是他所享受的。

normal.en: A passion for a hobby keeps the same shape: the interest takes hold of the person instead of the person holding it.
normal.cn: 对爱好的 passion 保持同一形状：是兴趣抓住了人，而不是人抓住了兴趣。

normal.en: Passion and enthusiasm are close, but passion is hotter and can include suffering, while enthusiasm is more often cheerful.
normal.cn: passion 与 enthusiasm 很近，但 passion 更炽烈，也可能带着痛苦，而 enthusiasm 通常更明朗。

normal.en: The idiom fly into a passion is old-fashioned; modern speakers usually say fly into a rage.
normal.cn: fly into a passion 这个说法已经过时，现代人多说 fly into a rage。

abstract.en: A word for suffering becoming a word for love suggests that deep feeling and pain were once thought to be the same event.
abstract.cn: 一个表示受苦的词变成了表示爱的词，说明深沉的情感与痛苦曾被看成同一件事。

abstract.en: We say a passion takes hold of us, never that we take hold of it, and that grammar quietly admits how little choice is involved.
abstract.cn: 我们说激情抓住了我们，从不说我们抓住了激情，这个语法细节悄悄承认了其中选择何其之少。

abstract.en: The Passion in a church and a passion for music share one root, which is why devotion can sound like a kind of endurance.
abstract.cn: 教堂里的受难与对音乐的酷爱共用一个词根，所以虔诚听起来可以像一种忍耐。

examples.en: She played the sonata with a passion that surprised her teacher.
examples.cn: 她以连老师都吃惊的激情演奏这首奏鸣曲。

examples.en: His passion for old maps began in a dusty second-hand bookshop.
examples.cn: 他对旧地图的酷爱始于一家满是灰尘的二手书店。

examples.en: He flew into a passion when the clerk questioned his account.
examples.cn: 店员质疑他的账目时，他勃然大怒。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「派神」——派神一投入就忘我，像被什么附了身；记住 passion 是激情、酷爱。

root: 来自拉丁语 pati（受苦、承受），经晚期拉丁语 passio（受苦）与古法语 passion 进入英语；与 patience、passive 同根，词义由「所受之苦」扩展到一切强烈情感。

sensesIntro.en: The core is something a person undergoes; the senses divide into strong feeling in general, an enduring enthusiasm, the suffering of Christ, and the old sense of a burst of anger.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是人承受的东西；义项按「一般的强烈情感」「持久的酷爱」「基督受难」「旧用法中的暴怒」分出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person bent over a piano, fingers pressing hard, shoulders trembling with the melody.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人伏在琴上，指尖用力，肩膀随旋律微微发抖。

branches.en: hands striking a keyboard too hard
branches.cn: 敲在琴键上过重的一双手

branches.en: a face flushed by feeling too large for speech
branches.cn: 因情感过盛而无言的一张脸

branches.en: a shelf of old maps collected for years
branches.cn: 多年收集的一架旧地图

branches.en: a candle carried through a dim church
branches.cn: 幽暗教堂里捧着的一支蜡烛

branches.en: a voice rising before the sentence ends
branches.cn: 话没说完就拔高的嗓门

intro.en: The word is built from the Latin verb for suffering plus a noun ending for a state, so its parts say a condition that a person is put in.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语表示「受苦」的动词加上表示状态的名词词尾构成，各部分说的是「人被打入的一种处境」。

latinIntro.en: Latin pati and passio are both recorded, and the English word follows them closely, so its Latin ancestry is reliable.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pati 与 passio 均有记录，英语词紧紧跟随它们，因此其拉丁世系是可靠的。

items.meaningCN: 由 com-（共同）加 passio 构成，义为「同情」

definition_zh: 技巧；技术；方法
definition_en: a special way of doing something that requires skill
core_image: 画者手腕一转，笔尖画出细线
scene: 她一遍遍练习运球的技巧。 She practised the dribbling technique again and again.
sceneCN: 这里 technique 是「技巧」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她一遍遍练习运球的技巧。

senses.title: A skilled way of doing
senses.definition: a particular way of doing something that needs practice
senses.definitionCN: 需要反复练习才能掌握的做事方式
senses.example: She practised the dribbling technique again and again.
senses.exampleCN: 她一遍遍练习运球的技巧。
senses.why: The root means craft, and a technique is the craft as it is actually done.
senses.whyCN: 词根意为手艺，technique 就是手艺在具体操作中的做法。

senses.title: A special method in an art or science
senses.definition: a recognized method used in art, medicine, or science
senses.definitionCN: 艺术、医学或科学中被认可的统一做法
senses.example: The surgeon learned a new technique for the operation.
senses.exampleCN: 这位外科医生学会了新的手术技法。
senses.why: Craft knowledge becomes a named method when a field agrees on it.
senses.whyCN: 当一门领域达成共识，手艺知识就成了有名字的「技法」。

intro.en: Technique came from French as the practical side of a craft.
intro.cn: technique 经法语进入英语，指手艺在实践中的一面。

items.en: Techne meant art, craft, and skill.
items.cn: techne 意为技艺、手艺与技能。

items.en: Technicus described something skilled.
items.cn: technicus 形容有技艺的事物。

items.en: Technique named a way of doing a craft.
items.cn: technique 指从事手艺的做法。

items.en: Technique entered English for skilled methods.
items.cn: technique 进入英语，指技巧性方法。

items.en: It spread to art, sport, and surgery.
items.cn: 它扩展到艺术、体育与外科。

note.en: Technique is compared with look-alike forms and with words for methods.
note.cn: 把 technique 与形近形式以及表示方法的词作对比。

entries.definition: of craft or machines
entries.definitionCN: 技术的

entries.definition: a skilled worker
entries.definitionCN: 技术员

entries.definition: plural of technique
entries.definitionCN: 多种技巧

entries.definition: a planned way of doing
entries.definitionCN: 方法

entries.definition: trained ability
entries.definitionCN: 技能

entries.definition: a way of dealing with something
entries.definitionCN: 途径

normalIntro.en: Technique is a craft made repeatable by practice.
normalIntro.cn: technique 是靠练习变得可重复的手艺。

normal.en: She practised the dribbling technique daily.
normal.cn: 她每天练习运球技巧。

normal.en: The surgeon learned a new technique.
normal.cn: 外科医生学会了一种新技法。

normal.en: Good technique saves energy.
normal.cn: 好的技巧能省力。

normal.en: Teachers share new techniques in class.
normal.cn: 老师们在课堂上分享新方法。

normal.en: His technique is simple but exact.
normal.cn: 他的技法简单却精确。

abstract.en: Technique turns luck into repetition.
abstract.cn: 技巧把运气变成可重复的动作。

abstract.en: A craft becomes teachable when it has a technique.
abstract.cn: 手艺有了技法才能被传授。

abstract.en: Precision is the signature of technique.
abstract.cn: 精确是技巧的签名。

examples.en: She practised the dribbling technique again and again.
examples.cn: 她一遍遍练习运球的技巧。

examples.en: The surgeon learned a new technique for the operation.
examples.cn: 这位外科医生学会了新的手术技法。

examples.en: Good technique saves energy.
examples.cn: 好的技巧能省力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「太克尼克」——把难「克」的动作练成习惯，就是技法。

root: 希腊语 techne（技艺）经拉丁语 technicus 与法语 technique 进入英语，指具体做法上的手艺。

sensesIntro.en: Technique is the practised way of doing a craft, and also the named method a field agrees on.
sensesIntro.cn: technique 是手艺中被练熟的做法，也是领域公认的有名方法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wrist turning to draw one clean line.
core.cn: 核心意象：手腕一转，画出干净的一笔。

branches.en: The practised way is the core.
branches.cn: 练熟的做法是核心。

branches.en: A field turns it into a method.
branches.cn: 领域把它固化为方法。

branches.en: Both depend on repeatable control.
branches.cn: 两者都依赖可重复的控制。

branches.en: Sport shows technique most plainly.
branches.cn: 体育最直白地展示技巧。

branches.en: Surgery needs named technique.
branches.cn: 外科需要有名有姓的技法。

intro.en: Technique shares the techne root with technical and technology.
intro.cn: technique 与 technical、technology 共享 techne 词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin technicus stands behind the French form technique.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 technicus 是法语 technique 的来源基础。

definition_zh: 部队；一群；成群结队地走；军队
definition_en: a group of soldiers, or a group of people or animals moving together
core_image: 一队人排着走，脚步一同落下，扬起一小片尘土
scene: 清晨的操场上，一排士兵沿着跑道走成一列，背囊轻轻晃动。 The troop moved slowly along the ridge at dawn.
sceneCN: 这里 troop 是「部队、一队士兵」（第 1 个义项：成队行动的军人）；句意为部队在黎明时沿山脊缓缓行进。整齐同行的一队人正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 名词加 -er 构成，义为「骑兵；州警」
现在分词名词化，义为「列队行进」
合成词，义为「运兵车；运兵舰」

senses.title: A group of soldiers
senses.definition: a group of soldiers, especially a unit of cavalry or a body of troops in action
senses.definitionCN: 一队士兵，尤指骑兵单位或行动中的队伍
senses.example: The troop was ordered back to the base.
senses.exampleCN: 这支部队被命令返回基地。
senses.why: A troop is first a small body of riders, and the word keeps that picture of a band moving as one.
senses.whyCN: troop 最初指一小队骑手，这个词始终保留「一伙人走成一体」的画面。

senses.title: Soldiers in general
senses.definition: soldiers considered as a body, especially those sent to a place
senses.definitionCN: 作为整体的士兵，尤指派往某地的兵力
senses.example: Troops were sent to the border.
senses.exampleCN: 部队被派往边境。
senses.why: The plural widens the single unit into the whole body of soldiers on a front.
senses.whyCN: 复数把单个单位扩展成前线上的全部兵力。

senses.title: A group of people or animals
senses.definition: a group of people or animals moving together
senses.definitionCN: 一起行动的一群人或一群动物
senses.example: A troop of schoolchildren crossed the square.
senses.exampleCN: 一群小学生穿过广场。
senses.why: A band of soldiers is a band, and any other band moving together borrows the name.
senses.whyCN: 一队士兵本就是一伙人，其他成伙走动的也用这个名字。

senses.title: To move in a group
senses.definition: to walk somewhere in a group, often without much order
senses.definitionCN: 成群地往某处走，常显得杂乱
senses.example: The children trooped into the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们成群地涌进礼堂。
senses.why: The verb is the noun set in motion: a troop walking becomes to troop.
senses.whyCN: 动词就是让名词走起来：一队人走路就成了 troop。

senses.title: A cavalry unit in the army
senses.definition: a small mounted or armoured unit forming part of a squadron or battalion
senses.definitionCN: 骑兵或装甲部队里的小单位，属中队或营建制
senses.example: The troop formed up at the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 这个骑兵连在门口集合。
senses.why: Military organisation keeps the oldest sense, a small body of riders.
senses.whyCN: 军队编制保留了最古老的义项：一小队骑手。

intro.en: The word comes from French troupe, a band or company, and is probably of Germanic origin.
intro.cn: 这个词来自法语 troupe（一伙、一队），大概源出日耳曼语。

items.en: Troupe means a band, a company, or a crowd, and is used of soldiers and of players.
items.cn: 法语 troupe 意为一伙、一队、一群人，既用于士兵也用于演员。

items.en: The French word probably goes back to a Germanic root meaning a crowd or a herd.
items.cn: 这个法语词可能追溯到日耳曼语里表示人群或畜群词根。

items.en: English borrows it in the sixteenth century for a body of soldiers.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入，指一队士兵。

items.en: The plural troops becomes the ordinary word for soldiers sent to a place.
items.cn: 其复数 troops 成了「派往某地的兵力」的通常说法。

items.en: The word also names a small cavalry unit and any group of animals or children.
items.cn: 这个词也指小型骑兵单位，以及任何一群动物或孩子。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the troupe spelling family, while the near-meaning group gathers other words for armed bodies and groups.
note.cn: 形近组同属 troupe 拼写家族，近义组汇集其他军队与群体的说法。

entries.definition: a company of actors or performers
entries.definitionCN: 剧团；演出团

entries.definition: a soldier in a cavalry or armoured unit
entries.definitionCN: 骑兵；州警

entries.definition: a curved shape closing on itself
entries.definitionCN: 环；圈

entries.definition: a prize won in a contest
entries.definitionCN: 奖品；战利品

entries.definition: the whole military force of a country
entries.definitionCN: 军队

entries.definition: a small organised part of an army
entries.definitionCN: 部队单位

entries.definition: a large number of people together
entries.definitionCN: 人群

entries.definition: a group of animals feeding or moving together
entries.definitionCN: 畜群

normalIntro.en: Troop and troupe are the same word split two ways: soldiers and players.
normalIntro.cn: troop 与 troupe 是同一个词的两条路：一边是兵，一边是演员。

normal.en: The plural troops is the everyday word for soldiers abroad.
normal.cn: 复数 troops 是「驻外部队」的日常说法。

normal.en: A trooper is the soldier in the troop.
normal.cn: trooper 就是队伍里的兵。

normal.en: Troupe keeps the French spelling for a company of actors.
normal.cn: troupe 保留法语拼法，指剧团。

normal.en: The verb usually goes with into or out of: they trooped out.
normal.cn: 动词常与 into 或 out of 连用：他们成群走出。

normal.en: A troop of monkeys works the same way as a troop of soldiers.
normal.cn: 一群猴子与一队士兵的用法相同。

abstract.en: Picture a line of soldiers walking a ridge at first light.
abstract.cn: 想象天刚亮时一列士兵走在山脊上。

abstract.en: Hear the boots land almost together.
abstract.cn: 听靴子几乎同时落地。

abstract.en: Then see a class of children do exactly the same on a stair.
abstract.cn: 再看一班孩子在同一段楼梯上做同样的动作。

examples.en: Fresh troops arrived at the front before winter.
examples.cn: 入冬前新部队抵达前线。

examples.en: A troop of monkeys crossed the road in single file.
examples.cn: 一群猴子排成一列过了马路。

examples.en: After the bell, the class trooped out into the yard.
examples.cn: 铃响后，全班成群涌到院子里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「出普」——一出营门就排成普普通通的一队人。

root: 法语 troupe（一伙、一队），可能源自日耳曼语「人群」词根，十六世纪进入英语；同族有 troupe、trooper

sensesIntro.en: Every sense names a body of beings moving together, from cavalry to schoolchildren.
sensesIntro.cn: 每个义项都指一起行动的一群，从骑兵到小学生。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: boots landing almost together along a ridge.
core.cn: 核心意象：靴子几乎同时落在山脊上。

branches.en: The soldier senses, where a small unit is meant.
branches.cn: 士兵义：指的是具体的小单位。

branches.en: The force sense, where the plural means all the soldiers there.
branches.cn: 兵力义：复数指当地全部士兵。

branches.en: The group sense, where children or animals form the band.
branches.cn: 群体义：孩子或动物组成这一伙。

branches.en: The verb sense, where the band starts walking.
branches.cn: 动词义：这一伙动起来了。

branches.en: The unit sense again, where the formation is what counts.
branches.cn: 再回单位义：关键在队形。

intro.en: The word is French in shape, and the family around it is small and concrete.
intro.cn: 这个词带法语形状，周围的词族小而具体。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin relative in English, so the Latin list here stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 它在英语里没有拉丁亲族，所以这里的拉丁同源词留空。

items.meaning: a vehicle or ship for soldiers
items.example: The troop carrier left at dawn.

items.meaning: to walk out in a group
items.example: They trooped out of the hall.

items.meaning: the ceremony of marching the colours
items.example: Trooping the colour is held in June.
items.exampleCN: 军旗列队仪式在六月举行。

definition_zh: 柜台；计数器；反对；反驳
definition_en: a long table where customers are served, a device that counts, or to speak or act against something
core_image: 一道长长的台面把顾客与货物分开，钱在台面上来回
scene: 售货员隔着玻璃台面递出车票，乘客把钱放进小托盘。 She paid at the counter and took her ticket.
sceneCN: 这里 counter 指「柜台」（第 1 个义项：商店或车站办理业务的长台）；句意是她在柜台付了钱，拿走了车票。

senses.title: The serving table
senses.definition: a long flat table in a shop, bank or station where customers are served
senses.definitionCN: 商店、银行或车站中接待顾客的长台
senses.example: She paid at the counter and took her ticket.
senses.exampleCN: 她在柜台付了钱，拿走了车票。
senses.why: A flat board is all that stands between a wish and a price.
senses.whyCN: 一块平平的台面，就是愿望与价格之间的全部距离。

senses.title: To speak against
senses.definition: to reply to an argument or action in order to oppose it
senses.definitionCN: 为反对某论点或行动而作出回应
senses.example: She countered his claim with a single fact.
senses.exampleCN: 她用一个事实反驳了他的说法。
senses.why: A blow can be answered by a blow that lands first.
senses.whyCN: 一拳打来，可以用先落下的一拳回应。

senses.title: A counting device
senses.definition: a small device or dial that records a number
senses.definitionCN: 记录数字的小装置或刻度盘
senses.example: The counter clicked past nine hundred.
senses.exampleCN: 计数器咔哒一声越过了九百。
senses.why: A machine counts so that a hand does not have to.
senses.whyCN: 机器来数，手就不必数了。

intro.en: Counter comes from Old French comptoir, a counting desk, from conter, to count, and Latin computare, to reckon.
intro.cn: counter 来自古法语 comptoir（算账的台子），源自 conter（计数）与拉丁语 computare（计算）。

items.en: Computare meant to reckon or add up.
items.cn: computare 意为计算或合计。

items.en: Conter meant to count or tell.
items.cn: conter 意为计数或讲述。

items.en: Comptoir named the desk where money was counted.
items.cn: comptoir 指数钱的台子。

items.en: English counter first named a shop table for money.
items.cn: 英语 counter 最初指商店里处理钱款的台子。

items.en: It now also means a counting device and a verbal reply against something.
items.cn: 今天它也指计数器，以及针对某事的言语回应。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the counting base count-, and the meaning group names other words for opposing and for a sales point.
note.cn: 形近组共享表示计数的词基 count-，近义组列出其他表示反对与售货点的说法。

entries.definition: to number or to matter
entries.definitionCN: 计数或显得重要

entries.definition: a local area with its own government
entries.definitionCN: 拥有本地政府的地方区域

entries.definition: to meet someone unexpectedly
entries.definitionCN: 意外遇到某人

entries.definition: to speak or act against something
entries.definitionCN: 出言或行动反对某事

entries.definition: to stand against a force
entries.definitionCN: 顶住一股力量

entries.definition: a small enclosed place for service or display
entries.definitionCN: 用于服务或展示的小隔间

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a long serving table, then move to a verbal answer and to a small clicking device.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一张长柜台开始，再到一句口头回击，最后到咔哒作响的小装置。

normal.en: A counter was once a desk for counting money, so the table keeps the name.
normal.cn: counter 原本是数钱的台子，所以柜台沿用了这个名字。

normal.en: To counter is to put a word on the other side of the scale.
normal.cn: 反驳就是把一句话放到天平的另一边。

normal.en: Over the counter medicine needs no prescription.
normal.cn: 柜台药不需要处方。

normal.en: Count plus -er gives both a person who counts and a thing that counts.
normal.cn: count 加 -er，既可以是数数的人，也可以是计数的东西。

normal.en: Counter- at the front of a word means against, as in counterattack.
normal.cn: 词首的 counter- 表示反对，如 counterattack。

abstract.en: Picture a glass top with coins on one side and goods on the other.
abstract.cn: 想象一块玻璃台面，一边是钱，一边是货。

abstract.en: Picture two arrows meeting head to head.
abstract.cn: 想象两支箭头头顶头撞在一起。

abstract.en: Picture a small wheel turning one tooth at a time.
abstract.cn: 想象一个小轮子一次转过一格。

examples.en: She paid at the counter and took her ticket.
examples.cn: 她在柜台付了钱，拿走了车票。

examples.en: She countered his claim with a single fact.
examples.cn: 她用一个事实反驳了他的说法。

examples.en: The counter clicked past nine hundred.
examples.cn: 计数器咔哒一声越过了九百。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 counter 记成 count（数）加 er：数钱数货的地方就是柜台，反过来顶回去就是反驳。

root: 源自拉丁语 computare（计算），经古法语 conter（计数）与 comptoir（算账台）进入英语，本指数钱的台子，后引申为计数器与反驳。

sensesIntro.en: From a table where money is counted, to a reply that counts against a claim, and at last to a device that counts alone.
sensesIntro.cn: 从数钱的台子，到针对某说法的回击，最后到独自计数的装置。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long flat counter with goods on one side and money on the other.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张长柜台，一边是货，一边是钱。

branches.en: The counter holds the exchange between buyer and seller.
branches.cn: 柜台承载买卖双方之间的交换。

branches.en: A reply pushes back against a claim.
branches.cn: 一句回应把某个说法顶回去。

branches.en: A device keeps the total without a human hand.
branches.cn: 装置不用人手就能记住总数。

branches.en: Both are places or things where counting happens.
branches.cn: 两者都是发生计数的地方或物件。

branches.en: To counter and to count both weigh one thing against another.
branches.cn: 反驳与计数，都是把一物与另一物相衡量。

intro.en: Counter is count plus -er, giving a person, a place or a device connected with counting.
intro.cn: counter 由 count 加 -er 构成，表示与计数有关的人、场所或装置。

latinIntro.en: The prefix counter- also means against, as in counteract and counterattack.
latinIntro.cn: 前缀 counter- 也表示反对，如 counteract 与 counterattack。

items.meaning: a table or device for counting
items.meaningCN: 用于计数的台子或装置

items.example: Countering the rumour took a week.

items.meaningCN: 用来反驳另一论点的论点

items.meaning: in the opposite direction to a clock

definition_zh: 职业；占领；占用；消遣
definition_en: a job or profession; the act of taking and holding a place; the use of a space or time

scene: 历史学家在旧档案里读到，这座城曾被外来军队控制多年。 The archive shows that the city lived through a long occupation.

derivatives.zh: 占据；占用；使忙于（由「抓住」义转来）

senses.title: A job or profession
senses.definition: the work a person does regularly to earn a living
senses.definitionCN: 一个人为谋生而长期从事的工作
senses.example: Her occupation is listed as laboratory technician.
senses.exampleCN: 她的职业登记为实验室技术员。
senses.why: a job takes up a person's time and attention, so the Latin verb for seizing a place was applied to seizing a day.
senses.whyCN: 工作会占去人的时间与精力，于是拉丁语中「占据地方」的动词被用来指「占去一天」。

senses.title: Military seizure and control of a place
senses.definition: the act of taking control of a country or region by armed force and staying there
senses.definitionCN: 以武力夺取并驻守控制某国或某地区的行为
senses.example: The museum closed during the occupation and lost part of its collection.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆在占领期间关闭，部分藏品散失。
senses.why: the core meaning is seizing and holding, which is exactly what an army does to a territory.
senses.whyCN: 核心义就是「夺取并占住」，这正是一支军队对一片土地所做的事。

senses.title: The act of filling or using a space
senses.definition: the act of taking up and using a building, room or piece of land
senses.definitionCN: 占用并使用某栋建筑、房间或一块土地的行为
senses.example: Occupation of the new wing begins in September.
senses.exampleCN: 新侧楼的启用入住从九月开始。
senses.why: from holding a territory to holding a room is a short step: in both cases something is taken and kept.
senses.whyCN: 从占住一片土地到占住一个房间只差一步：两件事都是「拿下来并保持住」。

senses.title: The state of being busy
senses.definition: the condition of being busy or having one's attention fully taken up
senses.definitionCN: 忙于某事、注意力被完全占去的状态
senses.example: He found occupation for his hands in repairing the fence.
senses.exampleCN: 他靠修篱笆让双手有事可做。
senses.why: the same verb can mean to keep someone busy, and the noun records that state of being taken up.
senses.whyCN: 同一动词也可表示「使人忙于某事」，名词便记录这种被占满的状态。

senses.title: Lawful possession of property
senses.definition: the legal holding or tenancy of land or buildings
senses.definitionCN: 对土地或建筑的合法持有或租用
senses.example: The tenant's occupation of the flat is protected by statute.
senses.exampleCN: 租客对该公寓的占有受法规保护。
senses.why: property law uses the word for the fact of holding premises, whether by owner or tenant.
senses.whyCN: 财产法用这个词指持有房屋这一事实，无论持有者是业主还是租客。

senses.title: A pastime that fills the time
senses.definition: an activity pursued for interest rather than for pay
senses.definitionCN: 出于兴趣而非报酬从事的活动
senses.example: Gardening is his favourite occupation on free afternoons.
senses.exampleCN: 园艺是他空闲下午最喜爱的消遣。
senses.why: because occupation means whatever takes up one's time, it covers unpaid hobbies as well as paid work.
senses.whyCN: 既然 occupation 指「占去时间的事」，它自然既包括有薪工作，也包括无偿爱好。

senses.title: Settlement of land by newcomers
senses.titleCN: 外来者对土地的定居占用
senses.definition: the settling and use of land by people who move onto it, often without formal title
senses.definitionCN: 迁入者定居并使用土地，常无正式产权
senses.example: Early occupation of the riverbank was informal and unrecorded.
senses.exampleCN: 河岸早期的占用是非正式的，也没有记录。
senses.why: history uses the word for land taken and held by settlers, keeping the original idea of seizure.
senses.whyCN: 历史叙述用这个词指移居者取得并占住的土地，保留了「夺取」的原义。

senses.title: Something that fills the mind
senses.definition: a thought, worry or interest that takes up one's mind
senses.definitionCN: 占去心思的想法、忧虑或兴趣
senses.example: The unfinished novel became his constant occupation.
senses.exampleCN: 那部未完成的小说成了他时刻挂心的事。
senses.why: the abstract sense treats the mind as a space that can be taken and held like a city.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义把心灵当作一块可以像城池一样被占据、被守住的空地。

intro.en: Occupation comes from Latin occupatio, from occupare 'to seize, take possession of', built on ob- 'against, over' and capere 'to take, grasp'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: occupation 来自拉丁 occupatio，源自动词 occupare「夺取、占有」，由 ob-「对着、在上」与 capere「拿、抓」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Capere meant 'to take, seize, grasp'. The Indo-European base often cited for it is a reconstruction, and related forms appear across the Italic languages.
items.cn: capere 意为「拿、夺取、抓」。常为其引用的印欧语词基属于重构形式，相关形态在意大利语族各语言中均有出现。

items.en: Ob- 'against, over' plus capere produced occupare 'to seize, take possession of, keep busy'.
items.cn: ob-「对着、在上」加 capere 构成 occupare「夺取、占有、使忙碌」。

items.en: The noun occupatio named the act of seizing and, by extension, whatever takes up one's time or attention.
items.cn: 名词 occupatio 指夺取行为，并引申指占去时间或注意力的事物。

items.en: Old French occupacion brought the word into English in the fourteenth century, first in the sense of holding a place or a post.
items.cn: 古法语 occupacion 在十四世纪把该词带入英语，最初指占住一个地方或职位。

items.en: War reporting fixed the military sense, while property law kept the older sense of lawful holding of premises.
items.cn: 战地报道固定了军事义，财产法则保留了「合法持有房屋」的旧义。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Latin shape of capere is reconstructed, and the exact force of ob- in this compound is debated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：capere 的拉丁语前形态属于重构形式，ob- 在该复合词中的确切作用仍有争论。

note.en: Group one holds forms built on the same Latin verb where the ending decides the meaning; group two holds words for the work someone does.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁动词、靠词尾区分意义的词形；第二组是表示「所从事的工作」的词。

entries.definition: To take and hold a place, fill a space or keep someone busy; the noun occupation is its action form.
entries.definitionCN: 指占据并保有某地、占满空间或使人忙碌；名词 occupation 是它的行为形式。

entries.definition: The person who is in and using a place at a given time, not the job that person does.
entries.definitionCN: 指某时正在使用某处的人，而不是此人所做的职业。

entries.definition: The state or rate of a place being used, as in hotel occupancy; it measures filling, not employment.
entries.definitionCN: 指某处被使用的状态或比率，如酒店入住率；衡量的是占用，不是就业。

entries.definition: Pre- 'beforehand' plus occupied: whose attention was taken up in advance, hence absent-minded.
entries.definitionCN: pre-「事先」加 occupied：注意力事先已被占去，因此显得心不在焉。

entries.definition: A job requiring specialised training and often a formal qualification, such as law or medicine.
entries.definitionCN: 需要专门训练、通常有正式资格的职位，如法律或医学。

entries.definition: The whole course of a person's working life, viewed as a progression rather than one job.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个人整个工作历程，被看作递进过程而非单一职位。

entries.definition: The state of having paid work, or the work itself; it stresses the employer relationship.
entries.definitionCN: 指拥有有薪工作的状态或该工作本身，强调雇佣关系。

entries.definition: A skilled craft or manual occupation, such as carpentry, often learned through apprenticeship.
entries.definitionCN: 指需要手艺的行业或体力职业，如木工，常通过学徒制习得。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real legal and military phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实法律与军事短语、真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: ob- 'over' + capere 'seize': to seize and hold, whether a city, a room or a whole day.
normal.cn: ob-「在上」+ capere「抓取」：抓住并占住，无论是一座城、一间屋还是一整天。

normal.en: The family runs occupy, occupant, occupancy, occupation, occupational.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 occupy、occupant、occupancy、occupation、occupational。

normal.en: The job sense survives in forms asking for your occupation at the bank or the clinic.
normal.cn: 职业义仍活在银行或诊所让你填写职业的表格里。

normal.en: Military phrases keep the original force: occupation forces, under occupation.
normal.cn: 军事短语保留了原义的力量：占领军、处于占领之下。

normal.en: Property law says occupation of the premises for the fact of holding a building.
normal.cn: 财产法用 occupation of the premises 指持有房屋这一事实。

abstract.en: Picture a chair pulled up to a desk and never moved, holding the same person for years.
abstract.cn: 想象一把拉到桌前的椅子多年不动，一直占着同一个人。

abstract.en: Picture a flag planted on a hill, and the ground beneath it is no longer freely entered.
abstract.cn: 想象一面插在山头的旗，旗下的土地从此不再可自由进入。

abstract.en: Picture a single idea sitting in a room of the mind and refusing to leave.
abstract.cn: 想象一个念头坐在心灵的某个房间里，不肯离开。

examples.en: Please state your name, age and occupation on the form.
examples.cn: 请在表格上填写姓名、年龄和职业。

examples.en: The occupation lasted seven years and ended with a treaty.
examples.cn: 占领持续了七年，以一项条约结束。

examples.en: Reading was her only occupation during the long recovery.
examples.cn: 在漫长的康复期间，阅读是她唯一的消遣。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「oc（一再）+ cup（杯子）+ ation」——一只杯子被反复占住 → 占据、职业

root: 拉丁 ob-「对着、在上」+ capere「抓取」→ occupare「夺取、占有」→ occupatio「占据；职业」。capere 的拉丁语前形态为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one act of seizing and holding: an army holds a country, a tenant holds a flat, a job holds a day, a hobby holds an afternoon, and finally a thought holds the mind.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕「夺取并占住」这一动作展开：军队占住国家，租客占住公寓，职业占去一天，爱好占去一个下午，最后是一个念头占住心灵。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand closing over a place and not letting go.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手合拢在一处地方上，不再松开。

branches.en: TAKING AND HOLDING LAND: armies and settlers both seize ground and stay on it.
branches.cn: 夺取并占住土地：军队与移居者都夺取地面并留在上面。

branches.en: HOLDING PREMISES: a room or a building can be occupied, lawfully or merely in fact.
branches.cn: 持有房屋：房间或建筑可以被占用，或合法，或仅成事实。

branches.en: WORK AS TAKING TIME: a job is what regularly takes up the greater part of the day.
branches.cn: 工作即占去时间：职业就是经常占去一天中大部分时间的事。

branches.en: FILLING TIME: being busy and pursuing a pastime are the same filling seen with and without pay.
branches.cn: 填满时间：忙碌与消遣是同一个「填满」，只是一个有报酬、一个没有。

branches.en: MIND AS TERRITORY: an idea can occupy the mind the way a garrison occupies a town.
branches.cn: 心灵即疆域：一个念头占据心灵，正如驻军占据城镇。

intro.en: Occupation is a Latin verb turned into an action noun: a prefix of direction, a root meaning 'seize', and a noun ending that English still uses productively.
intro.cn: occupation 是拉丁动词变来的行为名词：表方向的前缀、意为「抓取」的词根，以及英语仍能产的名称词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin capere supplies occupy, occupation, occupant, occupancy, capture, captive and capable; ob- adds direction or intensity.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 capere 衍生 occupy、occupation、occupant、occupancy、capture、captive 与 capable；ob- 增添方向或强度。

Occupancy fell after the new road opened.

items.meaningCN: 心事重重的；心不在焉的
items.example: He seemed preoccupied during the meeting.

definition_zh: 吨；大量；许多
definition_en: a unit of weight equal to 1,000 kilograms or a very large amount
core_image: 压秤的大铁块：一整吨沉甸甸的重量
scene: 仓库管理员看着进货单说： The truck delivered ten tons of steel today.
sceneCN: 这里 ton 是「吨」（第 1 个义项：重量单位）；句意是卡车今天运来了十吨钢材。

derivatives.zh: 由 ton 加名词后缀 -age 构成，义为「吨位；载重量」
公吨的英式拼法，与 ton 同源而用法有别

senses.title: A unit of weight
senses.definition: a unit for measuring weight, equal to 1,000 kilograms (metric ton) or 2,240 pounds (long ton)
senses.definitionCN: 计量重量的单位，公吨合一千公斤，长吨合两千二百四十磅
senses.example: The bridge can carry trucks up to forty tons.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥能承载四十吨以内的卡车。
senses.why: The core image of a huge heavy block is literally what the unit measures.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象的巨大重块正是这个单位所度量的东西。

senses.title: A very large amount
senses.definition: an informal way to say a very large quantity of something
senses.definitionCN: 口语中表示数量极多的说法
senses.example: Thanks a ton for helping me move house.
senses.exampleCN: 非常感谢你帮我搬家。
senses.why: Anything weighing a ton is enormous, so the unit became a hyperbole for plenty.
senses.whyCN: 重达一吨的东西必然极多，于是计量单位被夸张成「大量」。

intro.en: Ton comes from a Germanic word for a large cask, later fixed as a unit of weight.
intro.cn: ton 来自日耳曼语中指大酒桶的词，后来固定为重量单位。

items.en: Tunne meant a large cask or barrel for wine or beer.
items.cn: 古英语 tunne 指装酒的大桶。

items.en: The weight of a full cask of wine became a standard measure of about two thousand pounds.
items.cn: 中世纪英语中，一满桶酒的重量约两千磅，成为标准计量。

items.en: Ton was fixed as the unit of weight, spelled ton or tun.
items.cn: 十五世纪，ton 定型为重量单位，拼作 ton 或 tun。

items.en: The informal sense 'a lot' spread in everyday speech.
items.cn: 现代英语中「大量」的口语义普及开来。

items.en: The cask origin is generally accepted; early spelling varied widely.
items.cn: 「酒桶」来源一般被接受，早期拼写在历史上多有变化。

note.en: Words close to ton in spelling or sound, and words in the weight-and-quantity field.
note.cn: 与 ton 拼写或发音相近的词，以及同属重量与数量义场的词。

entries.definition: a large cask; an old unit for wine
entries.definitionCN: 大酒桶；旧制葡萄酒计量单位，与 ton 同源同音，只是保留了古拼写

entries.definition: a sound or quality of voice
entries.definitionCN: 音调；语气，只是与 ton 拼写相近，词源完全不同

entries.definition: the organ of taste and speech
entries.definitionCN: 舌头；语言，拼写与 ton 相近但词源无关

entries.definition: the metric ton, one thousand kilograms
entries.definitionCN: 公吨，与 ton 同指千公斤，只是英式区分拼法

entries.definition: a smaller unit of weight
entries.definitionCN: 磅，更小的重量单位，与 ton 构成度量阶梯

entries.definition: the base metric unit of mass
entries.definitionCN: 千克，公制质量基本单位，一千个千克合一吨

entries.definition: a quantity carried at one time
entries.definitionCN: 载荷；一次搬运的量，与「大量」义相通

entries.definition: a large untidy pile or quantity
entries.definitionCN: 一堆；大量，口语中同样表示极多

normalIntro.en: Anchor the word with its sound, its cask story, and its common phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 用发音、酒桶故事和常用搭配锚定这个词。

normal.en: ton sounds exactly like tun, the old cask
normal.cn: ton 与 tun 同音，tun 就是那只古英语大酒桶

normal.en: a full wine cask once weighed about a ton
normal.cn: 一满桶酒曾经就约重一吨，单位从实物而来

normal.en: tons of = a lot of in everyday speech
normal.cn: tons of 是口语中的「大量」，如 tons of time（大把时间）

normal.en: one metric ton = one thousand kilograms
normal.cn: 一公吨＝一千公斤，记住这个换算

normal.en: tonnage measures ships by tons
normal.cn: tonnage（吨位）用吨来衡量船舶大小

abstract.en: Picture a giant wine barrel slowly sinking a scale
abstract.cn: 想象一只巨大的酒桶把秤盘慢慢压到底

abstract.en: Hear the heavy thud of t-o-n dropping onto the floor
abstract.cn: 听 t-o-n 三个音像重物砸地的闷响

abstract.en: Feel a ton of homework pressing on your desk
abstract.cn: 感受一吨作业压在书桌上的分量，即「大量」义

examples.en: The elephant weighs several tons.
examples.cn: 大象重达数吨。

examples.en: We have tons of time before the train leaves.
examples.cn: 离火车出发还有大把时间。

examples.en: The ship has a tonnage of fifty thousand tons.
examples.cn: 这艘船的吨位是五万吨。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「桶」——ton 的发音就像「桶」，而它的词源恰好真是大酒桶；想象一桶酒重达一吨。

root: 日耳曼语源：古英语 tunne（大酒桶），一般认为源自中世纪拉丁语 tunna（桶），后者又可能借自凯尔特语。一满桶酒的重量演变为重量单位。

sensesIntro.en: A cask that once set a weight standard, now a unit and a byword for plenty.
sensesIntro.cn: 曾以酒桶定标准的计量单位，如今既是吨位又是「大量」的代名词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a giant cask pressing the scale down
core.cn: 核心意象：把秤盘压到底的巨型酒桶

branches.en: the official unit of weight
branches.cn: 正式的重量单位：吨

branches.en: informal talk about huge amounts
branches.cn: 口语里说「一大堆」的夸张说法

branches.en: from real tons to figurative tons
branches.cn: 从真实的吨到夸张的吨：一义两用

branches.en: hyperbole borrowed from heavy weight
branches.cn: 借用沉重感造出的夸张表达

branches.en: metric and long tons in trade
branches.cn: 贸易中公吨与长吨的区分

intro.en: Ton is a short borrowed noun with no living prefix or suffix inside it.
intro.cn: ton 是一个简短的借入名词，词内没有活用的前缀或后缀。

latinIntro.en: The likely Latin source tunna leaves few direct relatives in English.
latinIntro.cn: 可能的中世纪拉丁语来源 tunna 在英语中留下的直接同族词不多。

items.meaning: capacity of a ship in tons

items.meaningCN: 滋补品；补药，仅拼写相近，与 ton 无词源关系

definition_zh: 担忧；关心；涉及；关系；公司
definition_en: a feeling of worry, or something that affects or involves you
core_image: 母亲站在校门口，目光一直追着孩子的背影
scene: 医生看着检查单，眉头慢慢皱了起来。 The results concern me, so I want more tests.
sceneCN: 这里 concern 指「使担忧」（第 2 个义项：让人感到不安）；句意是这些结果让我担心，所以我想再做几项检查。

pos.zh: 担忧；关心；关切的事；公司

collocations.phrase: as far as I am concerned

senses.title: A feeling of worry
senses.definition: a feeling of worry about something important
senses.definitionCN: 对重要事物的担忧之情
senses.example: There is growing concern about air quality.
senses.exampleCN: 人们对空气质量的担忧与日俱增。
senses.why: When something matters, the mind keeps returning to it with unease.
senses.whyCN: 当某件事重要时，心就会带着不安一再回到它身上。

senses.title: To make someone worried
senses.definition: to make someone feel worried or anxious
senses.definitionCN: 使某人感到担心或不安
senses.example: The test results concern the doctor.
senses.exampleCN: 检查结果让医生担忧。
senses.why: A fact can reach out and trouble the person who learns it.
senses.whyCN: 一个事实能伸出去，扰动得知它的人。

senses.title: To be about or affect
senses.definition: to affect someone, or to be about a particular subject
senses.definitionCN: 影响某人，或关于某个主题
senses.example: This decision concerns every employee.
senses.exampleCN: 这个决定涉及每一位员工。
senses.why: What touches you is what you must care about, so concern also means involvement.
senses.whyCN: 触动你的东西就是你必须在意的，所以 concern 也指关涉。

intro.en: Concern comes from Latin concernere, to sift together, from com-, together, and cernere, to sift or judge.
intro.cn: concern 来自拉丁语 concernere（一起筛），由 com-（一起）与 cernere（筛、判断）构成。

items.en: Cernere meant to sift, to separate or to judge.
items.cn: cernere 意为筛、分辨或判断。

items.en: Concernere meant to sift things together into one view.
items.cn: concernere 意为把东西筛到一起，纳入同一视野。

items.en: Old French concerner meant to relate to or to touch.
items.cn: 古法语 concerner 意为与…相关或触及。

items.en: English concern first meant to be relevant to something.
items.cn: 英语 concern 最初指与某事相关。

items.en: The sense of worry grew from things that are relevant and important.
items.cn: 担忧义从相关且重要的事情中生长出来。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words close in shape to concern, and the meaning group names other words for worry and involvement.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 concern 形状相近的词，近义组列出其他表示担忧与关涉的词。

entries.definition: a public performance of music
entries.definitionCN: 音乐会

entries.definition: to notice something that is not obvious
entries.definitionCN: 辨认；察觉

entries.definition: about a particular subject
entries.definitionCN: 关于

entries.definition: a feeling that something bad may happen
entries.definitionCN: 担心；忧虑

entries.definition: the feeling that something matters to you
entries.definitionCN: 关心；在意

entries.definition: a feeling of wanting to know more
entries.definitionCN: 兴趣；关注

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a parent watching a child, then move to a doctor reading results and to a rule that touches everyone.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从母亲望着孩子开始，再走到医生看检查单与涉及每个人的规定。

normal.en: Con- is together and cern is to sift, so concern is what your mind keeps sifting over.
normal.cn: con- 是一起，cern 是筛，concern 就是心里反复筛检的那件事。

normal.en: Concern as a noun is the worry; concern as a verb is what causes it.
normal.cn: concern 作名词是担忧，作动词则是引起担忧的东西。

normal.en: As far as I am concerned means as far as this touches me.
normal.cn: 「as far as I am concerned」意为就触及我的范围而言。

normal.en: A going concern is a business that is still running.
normal.cn: a going concern 就是仍在运转的企业。

normal.en: Concerned parents ask questions; unconcerned ones do not.
normal.cn: 关心的父母会追问，漠不关心的则不会。

abstract.en: Picture a mother at the school gate watching one small back.
abstract.cn: 想象母亲在校门口望着一个小小的背影。

abstract.en: Picture a finger tracing a line of test results.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指沿着一行检查结果划过去。

abstract.en: Picture a circle drawn around everyone in a room.
abstract.cn: 想象一个圆圈把屋里每个人都圈了进去。

examples.en: There is real concern about the rising cost of housing.
examples.cn: 人们对住房成本上涨确有担忧。

examples.en: Her health concerns the whole family.
examples.cn: 她的健康让全家担忧。

examples.en: The new rules concern every member of staff.
examples.cn: 新规定涉及每一位员工。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 concern 记成 con（一起）加 cern（筛）：心里反复筛来筛去的那件事，就是担忧与关切。

root: 源自拉丁语 concernere（com 一起 + cernere 筛、判断），本义是把事物筛到一起加以分辨，后引申为涉及、关心与担忧。

sensesIntro.en: From something sifted into your view, to the worry it causes, and finally to the fact that it affects you.
sensesIntro.cn: 从被筛进你视野的事，到它引起的担忧，最后到它确实影响到你。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mother at the school gate, her eyes following one small figure.
core.cn: 核心意象：母亲站在校门口，目光追着一个小小的身影。

branches.en: The noun sense of worry is the most common in daily speech.
branches.cn: 名词的担忧义是日常口语中最常见的。

branches.en: The verb can point at the cause of worry rather than the feeling.
branches.cn: 动词可以指向担忧的起因，而非感受本身。

branches.en: Involvement is the oldest layer, still visible in concerning.
branches.cn: 关涉是最古老的一层，仍留在 concerning 里。

branches.en: Feeling and cause are two ends of one relation.
branches.cn: 感受与起因是同一关系两端。

branches.en: What touches you can worry you, and what worries you clearly touches you.
branches.cn: 触及你的事可能让你担忧，让你担忧的事必然触及你。

intro.en: Concern is built on Latin com-, together, plus cernere, to sift, through the French form concerner.
intro.cn: concern 由拉丁语 com-（一起）与 cernere（筛）构成，经法语 concerner 进入英语。

latinIntro.en: The Latin sift base cern- also gives discern, certain and discriminate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的筛分词基 cern- 还给出 discern、certain 与 discriminate。

items.example: The concerned neighbours called the police.
She asked a question concerning safety.
items.exampleCN: 她问了一个关于安全的问题。

items.example: He looked at the meter concernedly.
She seemed unconcerned by the delay.
items.exampleCN: 她似乎对延误毫不在意。
他的漠不关心让大家吃惊。

items.example: The concernment of the issue is clear.
items.exampleCN: 这个问题的重要性很清楚。

items.example: The concert raised money for the school.
